ದಿಕಲಂ^^^ಕಣಿಸಂವ್ಯಾನಾಮಗ್ರಾಹರಶ್ರಿಪ್ರತಾಪ | ಗ್ರಾಮಸಂಯು^®ಭಕರಸಂಪಾದ್ರಾತ ಟೂಕಾರಾಮಪೂರಿಭೂತಂ | ಮುಂಡರಯಾ^'ಮಕಸತ್ಯಸ್ಕಗ್ರಾಮಸ್ಯನಂದದದಯಾನಂ | ಸಂಮತ್ಯಾ^°ದೇವರಾಜಸ್ವಲಿಬ್ಯಕೇತಾಂಮುಕ್ಕಾಸನಂ | ಶ್ರೀಜೀಲಮಾ^ಹನಿಕೇಣಿಧಿವಸುವಾಹಹೇದುಂಗಣಿತವರ್ಚೇಧು | ಯಾಸ^^^ತೇಪುಜವತ್ಮಾನವೇಣ ವಂಗವಪೇಕ್ಷತ್ವಾ ಮಾನಿಸಪ್ಪುಣ್ಯೇ |^^^ಕೃಷ್ಣಸ್ಯ ಪಜ್ಞಗತಯಾಂಶುಕುದಂದನ್ಯಾಮಿನಿವದವಾಸರೇ |^4ಕುಚ್ಚೀಮಕರಸಂಕ್ರಾಂತಿಪುಣ್ಯಕಾಲೀಮನೋರಮೇ |^^^ಶ್ರೀಮದ್ಮದ್ಧಾಧಿರಾಜವೈಷ್ಣವಪಾಲಕರಮೇಶ್ವರೇ |^^^ಕಲ್ಯಾಣಜನಕೇರ್ತಿನಿವಿರಸ್ತತಪಜಾರದುಂಕಿತೆ |^^^ಆತ್ರೇಯಗೋತ್ರಸಂಜಾತತಾಳಲಾಯನಸನೂ^^ಸೃವಾನ | ಬೂಕಣ್ಣ ಬೀಟಾಮೌಜಸ್ಕಪ್ರಭಸ್ಸು^°ದ್ದು ಗೋವಾಧೀತೆ | ದೇವರಾಜಜ್ಯುತನಯೇದೇವರಾ"^ಜಮೂಪತಿ | ದೆಹಲಿಯೊಯುಳದನಾತ್ಯನೀಜ^°ವಿಕ್ರಮನಾಜಿತೇ | ನರಸಿಂಹಪುರಂಭವೃಣ್ಯಮು^^ಪಜೇಷ್ಠವಾಪ್ತಿಷ್ಟತೇ | ಸಾಲಗ್ರಾಮಾಧಿಪಾ^'ನಗ್ನಸ್ಗಾಮಸ್ಯನಕರವಿನೇ | ತವಿಕಾಕ^'^ಮುಕಾರಾಮವಇಲಿಷಕೇಕ್ಷಕಾಲಿನಂ | ಧನ^"^ಗೋಳದನಪನ್ಯೋಂಬುವಸಮಿಶ್ರಲಸ್ಮಿ*^ತಂ | ಭೂದೇವಕುಲವಾಸಸಾಧರಣಾಮವಮಂಜೂ^'^ರುನವಮಕರ | ಕೃತ್ಯೇಕಾವಿರತೀತ್ಯಸ್ತಿತ್ವಸ್ರ್ವೇನೆ ಪತ್ರದ ಹಿಂಭಾಗ,^ಕಾಮಮಪಲೋದಯಾ ! ವೇದಾಗವೇದವಿದ್ಯೋ ಪವಿತ್ರೇಪವಿತ್ರೇಣಿ*^ವಿಧೂತೇತ್ರುಸೂತ್ರಜ್ಞೇ | ಸದನ್ಯಪ್ಯೂಯುಷ್ಮಂ ತಾನ್ಯಪ್ಯೇ*°ಪೂವಿಕಾಸಸ್ಥ ಸಂಸ್ಥೇ | ನಾನಾವಿಧಾನಾಮವಮೃತ್ಯೇ^ಸಂಪಪತ್ಯೇಕಾವಿಂಕತಿವ್ಯಕ್ಷ | ವೃತ್ತಿಂಪ್ರವೃತ್ತೇಕಾವಕ್ಯ^°ಕಂವ್ಯಕ್ತೆ ಯುಕ್ತೇಶಿನಿಕೇತಸು | ಅಗ್ನಿ ಹೋತ್ರೇತ್ಕೃತಿಪಶ್ಚಾದಿಷ್ಠೇ^3ತಿರಂಗಗಳಸಂದಿಪ್ಯಾ | ಶ್ರೀಮನ್ಯಾರಾಯಣಪ್ರಶಸ್ತೀಪಾದಾ^ದ್ರಾಪದಪಸ್ರಣ | ವೃತ್ತಿಪ್ರತಿಗೃಹಿತ್ವಾಳಮೋಪೇಷಮಾ^ಗ್ರಿಹೋತ್ರಿ | ಗೋತ್ರಾಸೀನ ಗೋತ್ರಾಣಾಭಾನಾಚಿನೋಷೇಪಮು"6ತ್ರತ್ರಿವಿಸ್ತೇ | ಭಾರತದ್ವಾಜೋವಮಲಕಸ್ಮಕತ್ರಕೋರ್ವೇಂಕ"^ಟಿಶೇಜೆ | ದುಃಪರ್ವದಮಲೇಕಾಳಖ್ಯಿಸೋಮುಡುಯೇಕ್ರಾತ್ತಿ^^ಆತ್ರೇಯವ್ಯರೋಮಪಕ್ಷಜಾತಕಸ್ಮಕ್ಯ ಲೇಯಜಾ | ಯ^°ಜೀವವದ್ರಾಕ್ಶ್ಯ ಲೇಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ಸೋಮಮುದ್ಗ್ಯಾತ್ತೈಭೂಕ |"°ಲಿಂಗಾ ದ್ವಳೇಪಪತ್ಥೋರ್ಗತಮಗೋತ್ರೋಜೀಲಯಾ |^ಜಾಪೇದಾರಿ | ಹಮವಜೇವೈಪುತೋನೇನಿಕೇಚಿಯೆಜ್ಯಕಸ್ಮವೃತ್ತಿಯಡತೊರೆ ತಾಲೂಕು.ಮುಖಪದ್ಮ್ಯೇ | ಭಾರತದ್ಯಾಜ್ಞಾತ್ಪಶೃತ್ಪಾತ್ರ ಕ್ರೋಧರಾಮ | ಜಾಃ | ಶೂದ್ರೋಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣೂನೂಮಂತ ಸೋಮಯಾಜ್ಯೋತ್ಕೃತ್ತಿ ಭಾಕ | ಭಾರತದ್ಯಾಜ್ಞೆ ಓಮಯಾಯೂತ್ಪಾತ್ರೋ ಶ್ರೇಣಕಷ್ಟನ್ಯಜಾ |ಜೀವೇದೋದ್ಯಪೇಕುತ್ಪನ್ನೋಸೋಮಯಾಜ್ಯೋತ್ಕೃತ್ತಿ ಭಾಕ | ಪಾತ್ರೀಮಾಥ್ಯೋ ನಿರಪುಮಶ್ರಷ್ಟತನೋಯೇಚ್ಯಲ ಶರ್ಮಣಃ | ಸಾತೋ ಜ್ಞೆಯಗ್ರೀತೃ ನಂಜ್ಞಾಸೋಸೋಮಯಾಜ್ಯೋತ್ಕೃತ್ತಿ ಭಾಕ | ಬಸವಭಟ್ಟೋತೇತನಯೇಪ್ಯದ್ವಯಾರಾಜ್ಯೋಸೋಮಯಾಮಃ | ಹಾರಿತೋಯಾಜೂಷಾಣಪಾಥೋೇಲ್ಯೊಸಿಂಹಸ್ಯಕೃತ್ಯ ಭಾಕ | ಭಾರತದ್ಯಾಜ್ಞಿಮೂಲಾದ್ಯಾಪ್ಯಾತ್ರೋಶ್ರೇಣಕಷ್ಟಭಟ್ಟಜಾತಿಯೂವೇಣಕಷ್ಟಕಷ್ಟ್ಯಾಜ್ಯೋಯಪಾದ್ಯೇಪಶ್ವೀಕೃತ್ಯ ಭಾಕ | ಅಪ್ಪಲಾರೋಣ್ಯೋಪೇತ್ರ ಮುಂಭಾಗೀ |ಯೂಜುವೇದೀಯುಜ್ಜಾ ನಕಗೋತ್ರಕಸೀಪ್ಯುವಾಧವನೂತಃ |ಪಾತೋಯೇವೆಂಕಟನೃಸಿಂಹವೃತ್ತಿ ಭಾಕ | ಭಾರತದ್ಯಾಜ್ಞೇರಾಮನುಚಂದ್ರಪ್ರಕಾಶಸ್ಥ್ರೀನಿವಾಸಜ | ಯೂಜುವೇದೀಯಾಮನುಚಂದ್ರ್ಯಸೋಮಯಾಜ್ಯೋತ್ಕೃತ್ತಿ ಭಾಕ | ವೆಂಕಟಲಕ್ಷ್ಮರಾಯಪ್ರಸನ್ನ |ಜಾಕ್ಷೃಕತ್ತರಾಯಜ್ಞು | ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತಜ್ಞ್ಯ ಮಾರ್ಣದೇವನಿಸೂದಯಾಜೀವೇಕೃತ್ಯ ಭಾಕ | ಪಾತ್ರೋವೇಂಕಟಕಾಂತರಾಘವಸಾಧುಸಂ |ದರಾಯಜ್ಞು | ಭಾರತದ್ಯಾಜ್ಞೇಭಾತೃಕಾಂದವೀಕ್ಷಿತಸ್ಥ್ರೀ ವೀಕೃತ್ಯತ್ರೀಭಾಸ್ಯ | ರೋಗಾನಂದಯಾಜಸಾತ್ರೇಣ್ಯಸಿಂಹಸ್ಯತೂಯಾಜಾಪ | ಗೌತಮಲಾಲಭಟ್ಟಿನೃಸಿಂಹಕಾಮಕಾದ್ಯಾನೋಸೋಮಾಯ | ಅಬ್ದಾವಧಾನಿನಪಾತ್ರೇಕಾಣಲೀಯೋಯಾಜಪಹಸ್ಪದ್ವೀ | ಯುಲಂಷತ್ಸಯಸೂತೇಯೂಯಜಮಾಯೋಧ್ಯೇಕಹೃವೃತ್ತಿಭಾಕ | ಯಜ್ಞ ನಾರಾಯಣಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣೋಪುತ್ರೋರಮಣಕೋ |ದ್ವಿಜಃ | ವೃಸಂಹದೀಕ್ಷಿತಪ್ರಣೀತ್ಕೃಥಾಸೀಕ್ಕೃತ್ಯ ಭಾಕ |ಭೂಗೃಷ್ಟಿ ವೀರ್ ಲಭಟ್ಟಸ್ಥಗೀತೃವ್ಯತ್ರಕೋೇಳಗಾರಿಭೇಜ್ಞ್ಯ | ಶ್ರೀವಾತ್ಸಲ್ಯ ಜ್ಯೋತಿಮೇಶ್ವರ್ರೀ ವೆಂಕಟಕಾಂತರಾಕ್ಷಿತಃ | ಪರಾಶೃಪೂಯಜಪಹತೋಣೀವಿರಾವಾಧವಯಜಷ | ವೇಕಾಂಕಯ |ಯೂಜ್ಯೂಕೃತ್ಯತೋಹಾರಿತ್ರೇಯೂಯಾಜಪಹೂಸ್ಕೃತ್ತಿ ವೇ | ವತೇಯ್ಯೋಕಟಜಾಪುವ್ಯತ್ಕೋರಾಯಘವಜೋಸ್ಯತೇ | ಯಜ್ಞ ನಾರಾ |ಯಣನೀರ್ದೀಧನಾಂದೀಕ್ಷಿತಸ್ಯ ಕೃತ್ಯ ಭಾಕ | ನೃಸಿಂಹಸ್ಯತ್ರೀವೇಕ್ಷಕೃತ್ಯ ಭಾಕ ಋಭೂಪಣಣೋಯೂಮಪಾ | ಯುಜುವಿದ್ಯಾತ್ವ್ಯಾಕೃತ್ಯ ಭಾಕ 93 ಕರ್ನಾಟತ್ರಿನಿವಾನಸ್ಥನ್ಯಸ್ಕೃತ್ರಕಃ | ರಾಮಚಂದ್ರ್ಯ |ಸ್ಥ್ರೀಕೃತ್ಯವೃಟ್ಟಿ ದ್ವೀಣ್ಕಳಕವೀರಪ್ರದಿಕ್ಷಿತಃ | ಆತ್ರೇಯೂವೇಣೆಕಟಲ್ಲಸ್ವೀಪ್ಸಾತ್ರಕೋೇಣಸಿಂಹಸಂಜ | ಯೂಜುವೀಆರ್ಜೆಣೇಸ್ತಿ ಪತ್ರದ ಹಿಂಭಾಗೇ |97 ನಿಪಾತ್ರಾವಿಧೀಕ್ಷತ್ವ್ಯಕೃತ್ಯ ಭಾಕ | ವಿಕವಿಂಕತ್ರಿ ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಕಾ ವಾನಿತಾವೃತ್ತಿ ವಲ್ಲಭಾನಿ | ಅಥನೀೇಮಾನಿನಂದಯುಸ್ಲುಲಿಪ್ಯತೇದಳಖಾಣ್ಯಾಯ | ಮುಂಡುಲೀರಕತುಸ್ಥೃಮೋಯಲ ಕಲ್ಮಗಳಿವಾರ | ಮುಂಡುಲರಿಗಳಕಾಂಸ್ವಂತದಂಗೆವಾಯುಪ್ಪುನುಗಳವಾಡಿಗಳ್ಗೆ ಯೂಹಿದ್ದಾಗೆರಿಪುವಲಗಳಿಗಾವೂರಣ್ಯಮಗಳಮುದ್ದುಯೆಲ್ಲಿಗ್ರಾವಾಭಿಮುಖವಾಗಿನ್ನಿಳಾಮನುಮುದ್ರೇಕಲ್ಲಿ ೧ ಕಕ್ಕಲಗೆಂಕೆಲಸುದವನಕವೃತ್ತಿ ಅಲದಮದನವಿಜಪದಳ್ಳಿಯಳಿಗುಟ್ಟು ಕಲ್ಪನನ್ಮಂತ್ರಲಗಿನೆಪ್ಪಮ್ಮಮನಮದ್ಯೆಳ್ಳಗ | ಕಕ್ಕಲಿಗೇಂಕೆಲಸುಮಂಡೂರೋನಮದುಲತದಂಡಂಗವಲಾಳಗಿನೆಟ್ಟವಮನಮದ್ಮಳ್ಳಗ | ೧ ಕಕ್ಕಲಿಗೇಂಕೆಲಸುಕಲಡಹೂಡಿಕೆಕಲ್ಲುಗಂಗೆಗೆಬಡಗಳಿಗೇತವರಮೋಲನಿಲ್ಲೆ ಕೃವಮಾನಮದ್ಮ | ಕಳ್ಳಾ ಕೀಳಿಗೆಂಕಲುಮುಂಡುರಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಯೂತದವರಕಪಾರವಮಲಮುಂಡುರುಮುತ್ತು ಗೆ ಯಲ್ಲಿಕಳಕಾರವ್ಯುಲ್ಲಕಳ್ಳಿಕುಟ್ಟು ವರುಮದುಲಾವಕಕಟ್ಟೆಮೈಳಲಿಸ್ತವೃಪಮಾನಮದ್ರೇಳ್ಳು ೧ ಕಕ್ಕಳಿಜಡವಲಗಣಮಡೂಗೆರೀತೊೇಕಲಶವರದಳ್ಳೇದೃವಲಿನಿಕ್ಷೃವಮಾನಮದ್ರೇಳ್ಳು ೧ ಕಕ್ಕಳಿಗೆಸನೇ ಪತ್ರದ ಮುಂಭಾಗೇ |ಹಡುವೆಲುಮಡಿಗೆಬಹಳಾಗಿನಿದವಾನಿನಕಳ್ಳೆಸ್ಸೆವಮನುಮದ್ರೇಳ್ಳು ೧ ಕಕ್ಕಳಿಗೆಪಡುವಲುನೆಳಿಗೆಮೂದಲಾಗಿಬಳೆದೆವರವೇಟೆನಿನಿಚ್ಚುವಮಾನಮದ್ರೇಳ್ಳು ೧ ಕಕ್ಕಳಿಗೆಂಕಳುಪಿದ್ದಾಗೆರಿಬಡಗಳುಕಳಕಾರವ್ಯದದಹಳ್ಯಮೂಂಡುರಮುದ್ದು ಗೆಯೆಲ್ಲಿಗ್ಲೋಣಿಕವರದ೧ನಿನಪರವಿಲ್ಲೆಟ್ಟನಾಮನುಮದ್ರೇಳ್ಳು ೧ ಕಕ್ಕಳಿ೧ಗಡಾವಲುಮುಂಡೋಲಿಗನಿತುಯೆದ್ದಿಗೇಯೆಲ್ಲಿಯೇನ್ಯವಮಾನಮದ್ರೇಳ್ಳು ೧ ಕಕ್ಕಳಿಬೆಡ

cells.location: At Hebbasuru (Haradanahalli hobli), to the south of the entrance of the Rāmēsvara temple.
cells.remarks: A Temple erected by the Elkoti-dasa, having his head at the feet of S'iva, Kava-tamadi, son of Rabi-tamadi, son of Sava-tamadi of Marala.
cells.text_roman:
śrī-Marāla Sava-tamadiya maga Babi-tamadiya maga Kava-tamadi Sīvapada-sēkara Elakōtiya-dāsa

cells.remarks: Obeisance to Ganadhipati and S'ambhu. From Vishnu's lotus navel was born Brahma. In the world Achyuta (Krishna) was born to Yasoda and Nandagopa, and gave them a promise that he would eventually re-appear as a king to deliver the world when it was overspread by Mleschchhas. Accordingly he was born in the region of Pampa-puri to Sangama and his wife Kamambika, as Bukka-mahipati. He, with the assistance of Vidyatirtha-muni, became very great, the earth being as his wife, and the four oceans his treasury. Having freed from enemies a hundred royal cities counting from Dorasamudra, he ruled over an empire perfect in its seven parts. His son was Harihara, who was (next) established on the throne. Yedatore Taluq. The mahârâjâdhirâja râja-paramêsvara, subduer of hostile kings, punisher of kings who break their word, a light to the Sangamêsvara-kula, an ocean of all good qualities, the pârijâta sprung from the milk ocean of vîra-Bukka-Râja, promoter of the fortunes of all people, a royal bee at the lotus feet of (the god) Virûpâksha, famed for merit, of unrivalled valour, reverenced by all the world of kings, a Pâkâsâsana (Indra) to the circle of the earth surrounded by the four oceans, śrîmân Harihara-mahî- pâla, residing in the great royal city Vijayânagari, made a grant of the village of Hebasûr, with its 10 hamlets (named), belonging to Koṅgu-nâḍ, on the north bank of the Kâvêrî, in the Hoysaṇa country, forming them into an agrahâra named Bukkarâjapura, divided into three parts. And in order that his father the mahârâjâdhirâja râja-paramêsvara vîra-Bukka-Râja might obtain union with Śiva, and through the removal of his sins acquire the favour of Paramêsvari, bestowed it, with all the rights of possession, on Brahmans of all gôtras, (their names and boundaries of the villages given), appoint- ing as manager Dêvêśvara-paṇḍit, and giving him a one-third part. The forest fire rushing through the forest spares the roots, but the fire of a Brahman's property (if seized) burns up a race root and all. (signed) śrî-Virûpâksha.

cells.location: At Bherya (Mirle hobli), on a stone in front of the Anjaneya temple.
cells.remarks: Praise of Śambhu and Hari. (After the date), in the presence of the lotus feet of the god Raṅga- nâtha of the Gautama-kshetra, which is S'riraṅgapaṭṇa, situated in the middle of the Kâvêrî, the 60 Yedatore Taluq. rājādhirāja raja-paramêśvara vīra-pratāpa, champion over those that claim to have titles, possessing the title Dharani-varāha, champion over all . . . . . . chiefs, Dêva-Rāja-Odeyar's son, Dêva-Rāja-mahīpāla, while, seated on the throne of S'rīraṅgapattaṇa, ruling the kingdom of the world in peace, gave a stone charter for an agrahāra, as follows, to the village of Bhêryā established by himself, otherwise called Dêvarājapura. On this day, Dêva-Rāja-mahīpāla, son of Dêva-Rāja-Odeyar, and grandson of Chāma-Rāja-Odeyar, of the Ātrêya-gôtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra and . . . . . . śākhā, dividing the village of Bhêryā,—belonging to the new town of Narasiṁhapura, situated in the middle of the Kâvêri,—which had been inherited by his valour,—together with its twelve hamlets (named), this One Thousand place, into 92½ shares, and giving it the name of Dêvarājapura, he bestowed it upon Brāhmaṇas of all gôtras, sūtras and śākhās, all men of learning and worthy, together with gifts of elephants and horses, and many other gifts, with presentation of a coin and water, in order that Lakshmī-Nārāyaṇa may be propitious to us, and that our fathers and all our ancestors may attain to the unfading world of merit, with desire of making it an offering to Krishṇa, free of all imposts . . . . . . . . . . . .

Bhêryā,—belonging to the new town of Narasiṁhapura, situated in the middle of the Kâvêri,—which
had been inherited by his valour,—together with its twelve hamlets (named), this One Thousand place,
into 92½ shares, and giving it the name of Dêvarājapura, he bestowed it upon Brāhmaṇas of all gôtras,

cells.remarks: Praise of S'ambhu, Ganêśa and Varāha. To the south of Sumêru is the Karṇāṭa country, through which flows the Kâvêri, clothed with woods on both banks. There is the city of S'rīraṅgêśa, washed by its waves, and the king there seated on a secure throne was Dêva-Rāja-nṛipa. In order that his gifts might be perpetuated for a long time, he resolved to have a copper śāsana prepared, signed by his own hand, and containing verses relating to the history of his line. Of old to Chaturmukha, born from the lotus navel of Anantasāyi, the son was Atri. From whose eyes sprung Chandra (or the moon). In that (Lunar) race was born, as chief of Mahisha-puri, south of the Kâvêri, the king Chāma-Rāja. His son (with many praises) was Dêva-Rāja, who, by his wife Kempamāmbā, had a son Dêva-Rāja (also praised). All those that were persecuted by the Mlêchchhas, who had seized upon the land, flocked to him for protection. All kings, terrified at the mere sound of the bells on his elephants when he set out on an expedition, came and did obeisance to him. The Pāṇḍyas lost their kingdom; the Chōlas with all their forces sailed away to the islands; the Kēralas, losing their wits, took poison; the Haivas had all their efforts defeated by the gods; the Koṅkaṇas lost heart; the Hūṇas sought only to save their lives; the Habbusikas were pierced all over, and with their (gaping) wounds looked like the butea frondosa when in blossom. The Lāṭas were reduced to wander in forests; the Gurjaras were paralysed with the sound of drums; the Râṇas obtained nirvāṇa; the Kurus, Maravas, Mudgalas and Jaṅgalas, the Aṅgas, Vaṅgas, Kaliṅgas, the Magadha king, with the king of Madhura and others threw themselves at his feet. These exclamations (here follow various Mahratti and Hindustani expressions) were heard on all sides from those who fell in his wars. (After more praises) all the gifts described in the Hēmādri and other works had he made. In every village he established chatras for distribution of food, provided for daily festivals in the temples, and bestowed numberless villages as donations. In the holy bathing places of Prayāga, Gayā, Rāma- sētu, and the banks of the Gautami (or Gôdāvari), in Vēṅkaṭādri (Tirupati), and the city of Raṅga- dhāman (S'rīraṅgam), had he made many gifts. Dividing his kingdom into four parts, he gave the first to the Brāhmaṇas, the second to the gods, the third to charity, and reserved the fourth for his own use. (After the date, and praises of the Brahman donees, says) in order to form an agrahāra called after his own name, he made, as an offering to Krishṇa, a grant of the village of Bhêriya, together Yedatore Taluq. 61 with 12 hamlets (named) belonging to it, in the neighbourhood of Nrisimha-nagara (Holé-Narsipûr), in the Hoysaḷa-nâḍ country, acquired by the force of his own arm. To this village of Bhêriya, yielding altogether 1,000 niṣhkas, and filled with tanks and gardens, he gave the name of Dêvarâjapura, and divided it into 92 shares. And for the residence of the Brahmans he granted a site on the north bank of the Kâvêri, at Maṇikarṇikâ, east from (the temple of) Nrisimha, south of the Lôkapâvani, and west from Vêṅkatâdri (Karighaṭṭa); and establishing this place in the name of S'iva or Viśvêśa, he had 92 houses built there, 50 feet wide and 100 feet long, and with the usual ceremonies gave, to each of the Brahmans separately, one, filled with supplies for a year, together with jewels and cloths, and a cow in milk, with its calf. And in order to inform future kings of this grant he had it engraved in a śāsana accord- ing to the prescribed rules. (Here follow the names, &c., of the shareholders). Moreover, for recitation of the Vedas he assigned $3\frac{1}{2}$ shares. (signed) Śrî-Dêva-Râju.

text.location: On copper plates at the same village.*
text.remarks:
Praise of S'ambhu, Ganêśa and Varāha.

To the south of Sumêru is the Karṇāṭa country, through which flows the Kâvêri, clothed with
woods on both banks. There is the city of S'rīraṅgêśa, washed by its waves, and the king there seated
on a secure throne was Dêva-Rāja-nṛipa. In order that his gifts might be perpetuated for a long time,
he resolved to have a copper śāsana prepared, signed by his own hand, and containing verses relating
to the history of his line.

Of old to Chaturmukha, born from the lotus navel of Anantasāyi, the son was Atri. From whose
eyes sprung Chandra (or the moon). In that (Lunar) race was born, as chief of Mahisha-puri, south of
the Kâvêri, the king Chāma-Rāja. His son (with many praises) was Dêva-Rāja, who, by his wife
Kempamāmbā, had a son Dêva-Rāja (also praised). All those that were persecuted by the Mlêchchhas,
who had seized upon the land, flocked to him for protection. All kings, terrified at the mere sound
of the bells on his elephants when he set out on an expedition, came and did obeisance to him. The
Pāṇḍyas lost their kingdom; the Chōlas with all their forces sailed away to the islands; the Kēralas,
losing their wits, took poison; the Haivas had all their efforts defeated by the gods; the Koṅkaṇas
lost heart; the Hūṇas sought only to save their lives; the Habbusikas were pierced all over, and with
their (gaping) wounds looked like the butea frondosa when in blossom. The Lāṭas were reduced to
wander in forests; the Gurjaras were paralysed with the sound of drums; the Râṇas obtained
nirvāṇa; the Kurus, Maravas, Mudgalas and Jaṅgalas, the Aṅgas, Vaṅgas, Kaliṅgas, the Magadha
king, with the king of Madhura and others threw themselves at his feet. These exclamations (here
follow various Mahratti and Hindustani expressions) were heard on all sides from those who fell in
his wars.

(After more praises) all the gifts described in the Hēmādri and other works had he made. In
every village he established chatras for distribution of food, provided for daily festivals in the temples,
and bestowed numberless villages as donations. In the holy bathing places of Prayāga, Gayā, Rāma-
sētu, and the banks of the Gautami (or Gôdāvari), in Vēṅkaṭādri (Tirupati), and the city of Raṅga-
dhāman (S'rīraṅgam), had he made many gifts. Dividing his kingdom into four parts, he gave the
first to the Brāhmaṇas, the second to the gods, the third to charity, and reserved the fourth for his
own use.

(After the date, and praises of the Brahman donees, says) in order to form an agrahāra called
after his own name, he made, as an offering to Krishṇa, a grant of the village of Bhêriya, together

Yedatore Taluq. 61

with 12 hamlets (named) belonging to it, in the neighbourhood of Nrisimha-nagara (Holé-Narsipûr),
in the Hoysaḷa-nâḍ country, acquired by the force of his own arm. To this village of Bhêriya, yielding
altogether 1,000 niṣhkas, and filled with tanks and gardens, he gave the name of Dêvarâjapura, and
divided it into 92 shares.

And for the residence of the Brahmans he granted a site on the north bank of the Kâvêri, at
Maṇikarṇikâ, east from (the temple of) Nrisimha, south of the Lôkapâvani, and west from Vêṅkatâdri (Karighaṭṭa); and establishing this place in the name of S'iva or Viśvêśa, he had 92 houses built
there, 50 feet wide and 100 feet long, and with the usual ceremonies gave, to each of the Brahmans
separately, one, filled with supplies for a year, together with jewels and cloths, and a cow in milk,
with its calf. And in order to inform future kings of this grant he had it engraved in a śāsana accord-
ing to the prescribed rules. (Here follow the names, &c., of the shareholders). Moreover, for
recitation of the Vedas he assigned $3\frac{1}{2}$ shares.	(signed) Śrî-Dêva-Râju.Read more (4 KB)

cells.remarks: (Corresponds with No. 17 of this taluq, to Krishna-bhûpālaka.) In the line of the kings of Kalile (Kalale) was the king named S'rikanta. He had two sons, Nañja-Râja and Doddava, who, defeating many hostile kings, placed their left feet on their jewelled crowns. They had two sons, Basava-Râja and Vîra-Râja. Assuming the rank of commander of the army, Vîra-Râja increased the royal wealth by his valour, and bestowed the tulâ and other gifts on Brahmans. He had two sons, Dêva-Râja and Nañja-Râja (their praises). Dêva-Râja became the commander of the army of Krishṇa-mahîpati. He subdued and annexed Midigesi, Mâgadi, Sâvandi, and many other countries difficult to overcome. Nañja-Râja, whose father was Basava-Râja and his mother Mînanayana (Mînâkshi), became the sarvvâdhikâri to the same king. By the favour of Krishṇa-nripa, Vêṅkaṭapati was made the chief minister, and was said to be like the lips to Nañja-Râja and Dêva-Râja. By his consent, Nañja-Râja made all manner of gifts (named) to Brahmans. Having applied to the king Krishṇa for permission to make an agrahâra, containing 120 shares, in Kaṇvapuri, (after the date), the rājâdhirāja Krishṇa- Râja-mahîpati, son of Krishṇa-bhûpati, and grandson of Kaṇṭhirâvêndra, of the Âtrêya-gōtra and Âśvalâyana-sûtra, made a grant of Kaṇṇambâḍi (situation described), giving it the name of Nañjarâja- 62 Yedatore Taluq. samudra. And with each house, a mattress, a bolster and cot, with blankets of various colours, and stools for seats; vessels for worship, cows, and domestic vessels, filled with fine rice and the nine kinds of grain, jaggery, ghi, oil and other necessaries. And he honoured each Brahman with two cloths, a turban, a silk cloth, ruby earrings, rings and other ornaments. This agrahara of 120 shares, with 25$\frac{1}{2}$ hamlets, was given by Nanja-Raja (with all the rights and belongings as usual). (Details of shareholders, villages and boundaries follow). Last plates wanting.

cells.location: At Gaḷigekere (Tippūru hobli), on a stone near the village entrance.
cells.remarks: While the mahā-maṇḍalēśvara, the rājādhirāja rāja-paramēśvara vira-pratāpa Śrī-Raṅga-Dēva- mahārāya, seated on the jewelled throne in Penugonda, was ruling the kingdom of the world:— Venkatappa-Nayakayya, son of the Sindu-Govinda, champion over adulterers, a white-bodied Bhima, boon lord of Maninagapura, seizer of an expanded kingdom, defeater of the Turuka army, Bayyappa- Nayaka's (son) Krishnappa-Nayaka, gave to Vithala-Bhaṭṭa, son of Rāmachandra-Bhaṭṭa, of the Kāśya- pa-gōtra, Āpastamba-sūtra and Yajus-śākhā, a grant for an agrahara as follows:—Whereas we have repaired Galigekere, otherwise called the Râmapura agrahāra,—in Hampāpura-sthala, belonging to the Narasimhapura-sime, situated in the middle of the Kāvēri in the Hoysaṇa kingdom,—in order that merit may accrue to our mother Rāmamma, we (with names and titles as above) have bestowed it upon Vithala-Bhaṭṭa (described as above), in the presence of the god Narasimha on the bank of the Hêmâ- vati, free of all imposts and with exemption from hiring out, begging, tribute, exaction, assembly, hunting, forced labour, unpaid labour, customs dues, watch, these and all other troubles of $\overset{?}{\text{spear-}}$ men experienced by that village. The eight rights of full possession (named, as usual) within the four boundaries of this village of Râmapura, with power to mortgage, sell, give away or exchange, may you, your sons, grandsons and descendants enjoy in peace as long as sun and moon endure. (signed) śrī Veṅkaṭādri.
cells.text_roman:
Śubham astu svasti śrī jayābhyudaya-Śālivāhana-saka-varusha 1498 sanda mele vartamānav āda
Dhātu-samvatsarada Pushya-suddha 13 Saumya-vāsaradalu śrīman-mahā-maṇḍaleśvara śrīmad-rājādhī-
rāja rāja-parameśvara śrī-vīra-pratāpa Śrīraṅga-Deva-mahārāyaru Penugundiyali ratna-siṁhasanā-
rūḍhar āgi pṛithvī-rājyam geyyutt iralu śrīmalu Sindu-Govinda sitakara-gaṇḍa dhavalāṅka-Bhīma
Maṇinagapura-varādhīśvara bīru-saptāṅga-haraṇa Turuka-dala-vibhada śrī-Baiyyappa-Nāyakara
Krishnappa-Nāyakara komara Veṅkaṭappa-Nāyak-ayyanavaru Kāśyapa-gōtrada Āpastamba-sūtrada
Yajus-sākhādhyāyigal āda Rāmachandra-Bhaṭṭara makkalu Vithala-Bhaṭṭarige koṭṭa agrahāra-bhū-dāna-
dharma-sāsanada kramav entendare Hoysana-rājyada lam ... Kāveri-madhyada Narasimhapurada
simege saluva Hampapurada sthajada Galigekerege pratinamav āda Rāmapurav emba agrahāravanu
nā-jīrṇoddhāravanu māḍi namma tāyi Rāmammanavarige punyav āgakeñdu ondu a-grārāke uṇtada
bāḍi-bēdige-kanike-kaḍḍaya-kūṭa-bēṭe-bitti-bēgāra-suṅka-talavārike yivu moḍalada yiti-bādhegalu enu
yilla endu sarvamānyav āgi Bayiyappa-Nāyakara Krishnappa-Nāyakara komara Veṅkaṭappa-Nāyaka-
ayyanavaru Kāśyapa-gōtrada Āpastamba-sūtrada Yajus-sākheya Rāmachandra-Bhaṭṭara makkalu
Vithala-Bhaṭṭarige Hemavatiya-tiradalli śrī-Narasimha-devara sannidhiyalli Makara-saṅkrānti-puṇya-
kāladali namma tāyi Rāmammanavarige puṇyav āgabekendu nāu nimage i-Rāmapurav emba agrahāra-
vanu sa-hiraṇyōdaka-dāna-dhārā-pūrvakav āgi dhāreyan eṟndu koṭṭev āgi nīu nī-grāmake sahiva
chatus-sime-olagula nidhi-nikshepa-jala-pāshāna-akshiṇi-āgāmi-siddha-sādhyangaḷ emba ashṭa-bhōga-tēja-
svāmya-sahitavāgi nimage adhi-kraya-dāna-parivarttanakke yogyav āgi nīu nīmma putra-pautra-param-
pareyagi ā-chaṁdrār-sthāyigala-Agi nīu i-Rāmapuravanu sukhadalli anubhavisikoṇḍu bāhiri endu
Bayiyappa-Nāyakara Krishnappa-Nāyakara komara Veṅkaṭappa-Nāyak-ayyanavaru Kāśyapa-gōtrada
Āpastamba-sūtrada Yajus-sākheya Rāmachandra-Bhaṭṭara makkalu Vithala-Bhaṭṭarige koṭṭautha agrahāra-jīrṇoddhārada dharma-śāsana śrī-Veṅkaṭadri śrī śrī (usual final verses) i-dharmake avanan obbanu
alupidare tamma-tāyi-taṃdegala Vāranāsi vadhisi bhuuñjistā pāpakke hohannu mahi-mānake illadavanu
śrī

cells.location: At the same village, on copper plates found by Narasimha-Bhatta's raiyat in an old granary.
cells.remarks: Be it well. Success through the adorable Padmanābha, resembling (in colour) the cloudless sky. A sun illumining the clear firmament of the Jāhnavi (or Gaṅgā)-kula, possessed of strength and valour from the great pillar of stone divided with a single stroke of his sword, adorned with the ornament of a wound received in cutting down the hosts of his cruel enemies, of the Kâṇvāyanaśa- gōtra, was śrimat Koṅguṇivarmma-dharmma-mahâdhirâjah. His son, inheriting all the qualities of his father, possessing a character for learning and modesty, having obtained the honours of the kingdom only for the sake of the good government of his subjects, a touchstone for (testing) gold the learned and poets, skilled among those who expound and practice the science of politics, author of a treatise on the law of adoption (*dattaka sūtra*), was śrimān Mādhava-mahâdhīrâjah. His son, uniting all the qualities of his father and grandfather, having entered into war with many elephants (so that) his fame had tasted the waters of the four oceans, was śrimat Harivarmma- mahâdhīrâjah. His son, devoted to the worship of Brahmans, gurūs and gods, praising the feet of Nārāyaṇa, was śrimat Vishṇugōpa-mahâdhīrâjah. Yedatore Taluq. , 63 His son, whose head was purified by the pollen from the lotuses the feet of Tryambaka, having by personal strength and valour purchased his kingdom, daily eager to extricate the ox of merit from the thick mire of the Kali-yuga in which it had sunk, was śriman Mādhava-mahādhirājaḥ. His son, his mind illumined with the increase of learning and modesty, of indomitable bravery, was named śrīmad Avinita. His son, having the three powers of increase, who had brought anxiety to the face of Yama on account of the smallness of the residue left after the countless animals offered to him as a tribute (namely) the brave men consumed in the sacrifice of the face of the many wars waged for Andari, Alattūr, Porulare, Pelnagara and other places, author of a commentary on fifteen sarggas of the Kirātārjuniya, was named Durvvinīta. His son, the lotuses of whose feet were yellow with the swarming bees the lines of the crowns of savage kings rubbing against one another, was named Muṣkara. His son, of a pure wisdom acquired from his being the abode of fourteen branches of learning, distinguished for his skill among those who teach and practise the science of politics in all its branches, a rising sun in dispersing the clouds of darkness his enemies, had the illustrious name of Śrīvikrama. His son, whose broad chest bore on itself the emblems of victory in the shining scars of wounds received in many battles inflicted by the tusks darting like lightning of huge elephants, possessed of the essence of all the sciences, having gained the three objects of wordly pursuit, of virtuous life and daily increasing glory, was named Bhūvikrama. His son, uniting all the qualities of his father and grandfather, having entered into war with
many elephants (so that) his fame had tasted the waters of the four oceans, was śrimat Harivarmma-

His son, his mind illumined with the increase of learning and modesty, of indomitable bravery,
was named śrīmad Avinita.

account of the smallness of the residue left after the countless animals offered to him as a tribute

text.location: At Nēralāpura (Tippūru hobli), on a stone in a field, south-west of the village.
text.remarks:
While the strong-armed Vira-Ganga, the capturer of Talekâdu, Hoysala-Dêva, was ruling the king-
dom in the enjoyment of peace:—the great minister, Daṇḍanâyaka Bhôpaiyya, the governorship of
Bilivani Mahadeva in Tore-nâl having ceased, gave to Karekanta-Jiya certain land in Narasin-
ganahalli forest (boundaries described).

sishyaru Bayi-nada maha-prabhu Masaneyahaliya Kampana-Gavudaru tamage svargapavarga-nimittav

cells.text_original:
ಸರ್ಗೂರು ಹೋಬಳಿಯ ಸರಗೂರು ಗ್ರಾಮದ ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಪಂಚಬಸ್ತಿ ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ.
ಪ್ರಮಾಣ 5' 6" x 1' 6".
^1ಶ್ರೀಮದ್ವರಮಂಗಭಿರಸಕ್ಷಿದ್ಯು
^2ದಾಮೂಲಲಾಚ್ಛನಜೆಯೂತ ^ ) ಲೋಕನಾಥ
^3ಸ್ಯೆಸಾಸಕಂಜೆನಗಸನಂ || ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಶಕವರಷ ಇತಿ
^4ಖೆನವರ್ಷೊಭ್ಯಕ್ಷ ತಾಸಂವತ್ಸರವರಷಯಾ ಬಿಕು
^5ಗು ಗಂ | ಪ್ರಚಂಡದೋರ್ದಂಡಮಂಡಲೀಮಂಡನಮಂಡ
^6ಲಾಗ್ರ್ಯಎಂಡಿತಾರಾತ್ರಿ ಕಾಂಚಮಹಾಮಂಡಲೇಶ್ವರ
^7ಸಮುದ್ರಸಾವಾಧಿಪಲ್ಯಕ್ಕೇತುನವಿಜಯುಕ್ತರಾಯರಾ
^8 ಜ್ಯ್ಯಾಭ್ಯುದಯೋದ್ವೈಗದ್ಯೊಗದಹಸ್ತಪ್ರವರಕ್ಕೇಶ್ರೀಪಾದ
^9ಪದ್ಮರಾಧಕರದರ್ಪ್ಪ್ಯಿನನ್ಯಪಾವಧಾನಬಯಜಮದೇಂ
^10ದನಾಭರಪಹಾದಪೇಪೂಜೇವಿಸೆಕೆಯುಸಳರಾಜ್ಯ್ಯಾಧಿಸ
^11ತ್ರಿಣಾಗಣಮ್ಪೋಜೆಯರಮು, ಯೊಮಿಯುತ್ಪಾವತ್ಥ,
^12ತಾಪಹಾರ್ವರಮ್ಮ . ರೂಂದಲಂಗಣಗ್ಗಂತ್ಯಾ
^13ಪ್ಪ್ಯೀನೇಮತ್ವಪೀಠದೆಪವಯಾರದೆಪ್ಪ್ಯಾರಬುಯ
^14ನಾದಮಹಾಪ್ರಭುಮಗಹಣೆಯುಳಕಾತಂಕದ
^15ಣಿಗವದರುತಮಗ್ನಿಗಾಗರ್ಪವಗನಿಮಿತ್ತವಾಗಿ
^16ಳಜಳಳದೈೆಗ್ಗುಂಟುಮಬಾಸಾಸ್ವಾಮಿಗಳಅಂ
^17ಗರಂಗಭೋಗೇಸಂಗರಸತ್ಕರ್ಮಗವಾತದಂಬಬುರು
^18ನಾದಹಳಗತೊಂಟಟೂಸಣೆಯಯಾಗ್ರಮಂ ಅಜಹತುಃ
^19ಸೀಮೆಯೊಳಗಣಕೆರಗದ್ದೆಪ್ಪದ ಉತ್ತರೋತಮದಿ
^20ಕ್ಕಳಕಳಹೊಂಬಳಿಯೋಜೂನುಂ , ಉಜೊಂಬನು
^21ಪಿಂದಲಮಿಕ್ಕೇ ಹೊತಿವದಾರ್ಜೀತಸುವಾಸಿನಿಧಿ
^22ಪ್ಲಕ್ಷೀಪಜಲಮಾಪಾಣಮಂತದಾಗಕಲಸ್ವಂಮ್ಯದಕುಳ
^23ವನಸರುವಾರುಧರಾಣಾಚಕರ . ಯಲ್ಲಿನಾಗಣೆಬು
^24ಜಿಯೂರಕರಿಯಿಂಪುಬಿಟಿಸಿತ್ಯಾಸುಗುಮವಸನಾಥಸ್ವಾಮಿ
^25ಗ್ಗಾಗಳಕಡಪ್ಪಕ್ಕಳಸಲುಮತಾಗಗಿಂಜುಮಟಪ್ರರ
^26ವೆದಮಕೊಟ್ಟುವದಾನಲಶಾನ || ಸ್ಪದತ್ತಾ ೧ವರದತ್ತಾ ೦
^27 ವಾಯೋಹರೇತಪ್ರಸುಂಧರಾಂ | ಪಷ್ಮ್ಯಿವರ್ಷಾಸ
^28ಹಸ್ರಾಣಿವಿಷ್ಟ್ಯಾಯೂಜಾಯತೇಕೃಮ್ಮಿಂ || ಅಪ್ಪ್ಯ
^29ಯುಮವಿಖಿನಧಮ್ಮವೃರ್ವಾಮಿಕ್ಕೇಸಿರಕ್ಷಿಸುವುಂ
^30ಣ್ಣಾಪುರುಷರ್ಗಕ್ಕಂ || ಭಕ್ಕಿಯಿಪಾತವಸಂತಾನ
^31ಕ್ಷ್ಯಯುವಿಧಿಯ್ಮಕ್ಕಯಂಕ್ಯುಲಕಮ್ಯು ||
^32ದಾನಪವಲನೆಯೊಮ್ಮ್ಯದಣ್ಮಡನಾಥಕ್ರೇಯೊನುಪವ
^33ಲನಂ | ದಾನಾತಗ್ಗನ್ಯಗವಮವಸ್ಪು ಪ್ರಪಾಲನಮದುತ್ಯತೇ
^34ಪದಂ || ಸೌಮ್ಯಸನ್ಯೊಯುದಮಧ್ಯಸೇಸೇತನ್ಯಸ್ವಾಸ್ತಂಗಂ
^35ಕಾಲಿಕಾಲೇಪಾ ನೀಯೊಭೂಧವವಕ್ಕಿ | ಇಥಂಭೂತಾಭಾ
^36ವಿನಪಾರ್ಧಿವೇಂದ್ರಾನ್ಭಯೋಯೋಯೋಜೆಯಾತೇಚೆಪ್ರಾ
^37 ವಚೆಶಂದ್ರೃ ||

text.text_original: ಸರ್ಗೂರು ಹೋಬಳಿಯ ಸರಗೂರು ಗ್ರಾಮದ ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಪಂಚಬಸ್ತಿ ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ.ಪ್ರಮಾಣ 5' 6" x 1' 6".^1ಶ್ರೀಮದ್ವರಮಂಗಭಿರಸಕ್ಷಿದ್ಯು^2ದಾಮೂಲಲಾಚ್ಛನಜೆಯೂತ ^ ) ಲೋಕನಾಥ^3ಸ್ಯೆಸಾಸಕಂಜೆನಗಸನಂ || ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಶಕವರಷ ಇತಿ^4ಖೆನವರ್ಷೊಭ್ಯಕ್ಷ ತಾಸಂವತ್ಸರವರಷಯಾ ಬಿಕು^5ಗು ಗಂ | ಪ್ರಚಂಡದೋರ್ದಂಡಮಂಡಲೀಮಂಡನಮಂಡ^6ಲಾಗ್ರ್ಯಎಂಡಿತಾರಾತ್ರಿ ಕಾಂಚಮಹಾಮಂಡಲೇಶ್ವರ^7ಸಮುದ್ರಸಾವಾಧಿಪಲ್ಯಕ್ಕೇತುನವಿಜಯುಕ್ತರಾಯರಾ^8 ಜ್ಯ್ಯಾಭ್ಯುದಯೋದ್ವೈಗದ್ಯೊಗದಹಸ್ತಪ್ರವರಕ್ಕೇಶ್ರೀಪಾದ^9ಪದ್ಮರಾಧಕರದರ್ಪ್ಪ್ಯಿನನ್ಯಪಾವಧಾನಬಯಜಮದೇಂ^10ದನಾಭರಪಹಾದಪೇಪೂಜೇವಿಸೆಕೆಯುಸಳರಾಜ್ಯ್ಯಾಧಿಸ^11ತ್ರಿಣಾಗಣಮ್ಪೋಜೆಯರಮು, ಯೊಮಿಯುತ್ಪಾವತ್ಥ,^12ತಾಪಹಾರ್ವರಮ್ಮ . ರೂಂದಲಂಗಣಗ್ಗಂತ್ಯಾ^13ಪ್ಪ್ಯೀನೇಮತ್ವಪೀಠದೆಪವಯಾರದೆಪ್ಪ್ಯಾರಬುಯ^14ನಾದಮಹಾಪ್ರಭುಮಗಹಣೆಯುಳಕಾತಂಕದ^15ಣಿಗವದರುತಮಗ್ನಿಗಾಗರ್ಪವಗನಿಮಿತ್ತವಾಗಿ^16ಳಜಳಳದೈೆಗ್ಗುಂಟುಮಬಾಸಾಸ್ವಾಮಿಗಳಅಂ^17ಗರಂಗಭೋಗೇಸಂಗರಸತ್ಕರ್ಮಗವಾತದಂಬಬುರು^18ನಾದಹಳಗತೊಂಟಟೂಸಣೆಯಯಾಗ್ರಮಂ ಅಜಹತುಃ^19ಸೀಮೆಯೊಳಗಣಕೆರಗದ್ದೆಪ್ಪದ ಉತ್ತರೋತಮದಿ^20ಕ್ಕಳಕಳಹೊಂಬಳಿಯೋಜೂನುಂ , ಉಜೊಂಬನು^21ಪಿಂದಲಮಿಕ್ಕೇ ಹೊತಿವದಾರ್ಜೀತಸುವಾಸಿನಿಧಿ^22ಪ್ಲಕ್ಷೀಪಜಲಮಾಪಾಣಮಂತದಾಗಕಲಸ್ವಂಮ್ಯದಕುಳ^23ವನಸರುವಾರುಧರಾಣಾಚಕರ . ಯಲ್ಲಿನಾಗಣೆಬು^24ಜಿಯೂರಕರಿಯಿಂಪುಬಿಟಿಸಿತ್ಯಾಸುಗುಮವಸನಾಥಸ್ವಾಮಿ^25ಗ್ಗಾಗಳಕಡಪ್ಪಕ್ಕಳಸಲುಮತಾಗಗಿಂಜುಮಟಪ್ರರ^26ವೆದಮಕೊಟ್ಟುವದಾನಲಶಾನ || ಸ್ಪದತ್ತಾ ೧ವರದತ್ತಾ ೦^27 ವಾಯೋಹರೇತಪ್ರಸುಂಧರಾಂ | ಪಷ್ಮ್ಯಿವರ್ಷಾಸ^28ಹಸ್ರಾಣಿವಿಷ್ಟ್ಯಾಯೂಜಾಯತೇಕೃಮ್ಮಿಂ || ಅಪ್ಪ್ಯ^29ಯುಮವಿಖಿನಧಮ್ಮವೃರ್ವಾಮಿಕ್ಕೇಸಿರಕ್ಷಿಸುವುಂ^30ಣ್ಣಾಪುರುಷರ್ಗಕ್ಕಂ || ಭಕ್ಕಿಯಿಪಾತವಸಂತಾನ^31ಕ್ಷ್ಯಯುವಿಧಿಯ್ಮಕ್ಕಯಂಕ್ಯುಲಕಮ್ಯು ||^32ದಾನಪವಲನೆಯೊಮ್ಮ್ಯದಣ್ಮಡನಾಥಕ್ರೇಯೊನುಪವ^33ಲನಂ | ದಾನಾತಗ್ಗನ್ಯಗವಮವಸ್ಪು ಪ್ರಪಾಲನಮದುತ್ಯತೇ^34ಪದಂ || ಸೌಮ್ಯಸನ್ಯೊಯುದಮಧ್ಯಸೇಸೇತನ್ಯಸ್ವಾಸ್ತಂಗಂ^35ಕಾಲಿಕಾಲೇಪಾ ನೀಯೊಭೂಧವವಕ್ಕಿ | ಇಥಂಭೂತಾಭಾ^36ವಿನಪಾರ್ಧಿವೇಂದ್ರಾನ್ಭಯೋಯೋಯೋಜೆಯಾತೇಚೆಪ್ರಾ^37 ವಚೆಶಂದ್ರೃ ||

cells.remarks: While Kongaṇivarmma dharmma-mahārājādhirāja paramēśvara Śripuruṣha-mahārāja was ruling the kingdom of the world :—Kesugolam-Ôḍeya gave Dharmagavāḍi to Biṇamma as a Brahman gift, At the śri-nakshatra of S'ripurusha's bhātāra, twelve Brahmans will be fed for a month. (The grant is) for one life. The tax on this is ten gadlyāṇa a year. Its boundaries (given). Usual imprecation. By (order of) Prithvi-Koṅgaṇi-mahārāja, whose first name was S'ripuruṣha, the middle of whose palace continually resounded with the holy rites accompanying his daily rich gifts,—his great feudatory Mada-Koṅguṇi-Yediyarasa, governing the Aridālkôse Seventy and the lands belonging to it, having made request to S'ripuruṣha-mahārāja,—Kesugolam-Ôḍeya presented Pervattiyur and Marddûr to the Brah- mans as a Brahman gift. Their produce—from Pervattiyur the rent is two ? Peṇṇanḍi ; the rent of Mardûr is twelve paṇa in cash and twelve khandugas of rice. Their boundaries (described). 66 Heggadadevanakote Taluq. Written by Kuntachâryya. The Brahmans of Kesugola gave to Nandigunda a gift of one aḍuvu (grazing land) in Mardûr.

cells.location: At S'aṅkahalli (Saraguru hobli), on a stone at the village entrance.
cells.remarks: The rājādhirāja Krishna-Rāja-Vodeyar of Mahasûr has this day made to Venkata-Subbaiya, court professor of the vine, a grant of the village of Sâṅkhahalli, with the presentation of a coin and pouring of water, as an offering to Krishna: wherefore, that you, your sons grandsons and posterity, may con- tinue to enjoy this as long as sun and moon endure, has this rent-free charter been written and given.

^1ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ[ಶ್ರೀಮತ್ತುಪನಾ[ಪೇ]ಕ್ಷಕನ್ವತಿ ರವಿಗರಮೇಶ್ವರದೇವನರುಕಾನ್ಯನೂರೆಳ
^2ಗಿಪ [ವಿ]ರಾಜ್ಯಂಗೆಯ್ಯುತ್ತಿ ರಲ್ಕೇವನ್ಮಹಾಪ್ರಧಾನಸಂಸ್ವಾಧಿ ಕಾರಿರುಪತರಾ
^3ಯತುಳಸೀವೇದಾಣ್ಯದರ್ಕಳೀತಕರದೇವನ[ಪ]ರಪುಸಾಹತದ
^4ನೂಜೆಯ್ಪೆತ್ತಿಂತನೆವರಾಕ್ಷಸವತ್ಸರದವಸಡಸದ್ಮಚತುದ್ದಿಸಿಲಿದಿವಾ
^5ರೆಮುಮನಕ್ಷ್ಮಾವೆತ್ತಯೋಳಗದಂಖ್ಯುಮತುನಿಳಿಗಲಿಸಾಧುರಕಣಿಯು
^6ಉಟಿಕಷಮತಿವೇದವಾಪೋಣಪರಂಗೋಮಾವರುನಯಾಕುರುಸಿ ರದಜ್ಯಂಗ್ಯುತ್ತಿ ರಲು
^7ನಾಗುನಾಜಪಳಶತರಸನ್ನಾಸಪತಿಎಕ್ಕಣಿಪಂಡಿತರುನುಷ್ಯತಿ ಕೊಡೆಯೆಸು
^8ಪುತ್ರನಾರಾಹಮಲಣ್ಣ ಜೆಯಿಉತಮಯ್ಯಾಜಿನವಡಿದೇವಳಿಕೆ ಇಡಹೊ
^9ನಿಗೆಹದುಮನಾಕೇಯಳವರುತ್ತೊಹಡೇತಿ ದೇವವಧಿ ಕತ್ರ್ಯ ಕಾಂಕ್ಷ್ಯದಪೂಜ
^10ಪ್ಪುತ್ತ ನಿಕ್ಕಿ ನಗುನಜಡಹಟ್ಟಯಮುದೇವಪಿನಮಾಗರವದಹಣ=ಳತುರೋಜೇಳದೇ
^11ವನಮಗಹೋಯದ್ಯುದೇವಪಸವಚೀದೆವನರುಗದದೇವೇವಮನವರಕವ್ಯಾಯ
^12ಉಪ್ಪ ಸಹಿತವರ್ಗಾವಾತೆಡಹಕತುಬಾಲಂಶಗಾಸಮಗಮವಗಮನಿಡಿಕೊಡುವು
^13ಕ್ಲಿ ಕಾಜಾ ರಣಾವೀ ಈಸ್ವರದೆವರುಕಾತೇನವತ್ಯು ಯಬಳಗೆಸಂದಯಮತವಯ್ಯಚಿ
^14ಕಜೆಟಮಣ್ಣಿ ಹರುವವಡೀಗಳತುರಮುಡಿಕಾಫ್ ನದೇವಮನುಮಹಿಸನ
^15ಹೊಮ್ಯುನಿನಿಸಿದನಸನಕಲಮಂಗಳಮಹಾಸ್ರಿ ಶ್ರಿ ಶ್ರಿ ಮಾದಯ್ಯನ
^16ಪುಲುವನಸಿಪಸಹಜವಿನಸಹಜವಗವರಿದನುಮಂತಬಳಿಕೆಕನಿಸಿವಸಿ
^17ಮಡಿನಿನಿಸಿದಸನಗಲಹಿಸಿಕೊಡಮಕ್ಷ ಳಕಲುದವೇದವಾಳಿಕೆಗಮನನಬತ
^18ವೆಂಕುಜಾವದರೆಇಕಳಕಲಿದುಕುಹೂನುಸನಗಲಿಗೆಹೆಃ .ದಹಟುಜನಮಹಾಸನಕೋ
^19ಜಮಮುತನ್ಯ ಜೊನೆಳಗೆಸಲುಪವಡೆಯುಸಃಕಿಯುತತೆಹೊನಪೂತ್ಹು || ಮಗಸಕೊಜ್ಞ
^20ಚಿಕೊಡಿಯುನುದನೆಯ್ಕತ್ತೆ ತ್ತಿ ದ್ಧಿ ನುತನವದಿಡಗೆಸಕ್ಷಿ ಅದೆವಲ್ಕೇಕಳು
^21ಕೇತರಪಳಯಉಯಿಗಮಉಡಜನವಮರ್ಕಳಿಗೆಉಪಬೆಟ್ಟು. ಹಣ್ಣಿಯನುಮಕಿ ದೇವಮನಗರಾಮು.
^22ಚೇಜೆವಕೋಳಳದೇವವನಗರಕೋಡಿನವಡಮತಿದೇವವನಮಸುಂಜೇದೆ[ಪೋರೆಣೇಕ್ಕ ನಸೇನಜೋವ
^23ವಮಧುಮ್ಮನಸುದಾಯಯನಕನಸಿಯಿಸಿಸಗರಬೆರುದ

text.text_original: ಅದೇ ಪೋಚಬಾಳೇತುರು ಗ್ರಾಮದ ಮಲ್ಲೇಶ್ವರಗುಡಿಯ ಒಳಗೆ ನೆಟ್ಟ ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ.ಪಮಾಣ 2′ 6″ × 2′ 10″.^1ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ[ಶ್ರೀಮತ್ತುಪನಾ[ಪೇ]ಕ್ಷಕನ್ವತಿ ರವಿಗರಮೇಶ್ವರದೇವನರುಕಾನ್ಯನೂರೆಳ^2ಗಿಪ [ವಿ]ರಾಜ್ಯಂಗೆಯ್ಯುತ್ತಿ ರಲ್ಕೇವನ್ಮಹಾಪ್ರಧಾನಸಂಸ್ವಾಧಿ ಕಾರಿರುಪತರಾ^3ಯತುಳಸೀವೇದಾಣ್ಯದರ್ಕಳೀತಕರದೇವನ[ಪ]ರಪುಸಾಹತದ^4ನೂಜೆಯ್ಪೆತ್ತಿಂತನೆವರಾಕ್ಷಸವತ್ಸರದವಸಡಸದ್ಮಚತುದ್ದಿಸಿಲಿದಿವಾ^5ರೆಮುಮನಕ್ಷ್ಮಾವೆತ್ತಯೋಳಗದಂಖ್ಯುಮತುನಿಳಿಗಲಿಸಾಧುರಕಣಿಯು^6ಉಟಿಕಷಮತಿವೇದವಾಪೋಣಪರಂಗೋಮಾವರುನಯಾಕುರುಸಿ ರದಜ್ಯಂಗ್ಯುತ್ತಿ ರಲು^7ನಾಗುನಾಜಪಳಶತರಸನ್ನಾಸಪತಿಎಕ್ಕಣಿಪಂಡಿತರುನುಷ್ಯತಿ ಕೊಡೆಯೆಸು^8ಪುತ್ರನಾರಾಹಮಲಣ್ಣ ಜೆಯಿಉತಮಯ್ಯಾಜಿನವಡಿದೇವಳಿಕೆ ಇಡಹೊ^9ನಿಗೆಹದುಮನಾಕೇಯಳವರುತ್ತೊಹಡೇತಿ ದೇವವಧಿ ಕತ್ರ್ಯ ಕಾಂಕ್ಷ್ಯದಪೂಜ^10ಪ್ಪುತ್ತ ನಿಕ್ಕಿ ನಗುನಜಡಹಟ್ಟಯಮುದೇವಪಿನಮಾಗರವದಹಣ=ಳತುರೋಜೇಳದೇ^11ವನಮಗಹೋಯದ್ಯುದೇವಪಸವಚೀದೆವನರುಗದದೇವೇವಮನವರಕವ್ಯಾಯ^12ಉಪ್ಪ ಸಹಿತವರ್ಗಾವಾತೆಡಹಕತುಬಾಲಂಶಗಾಸಮಗಮವಗಮನಿಡಿಕೊಡುವು^13ಕ್ಲಿ ಕಾಜಾ ರಣಾವೀ ಈಸ್ವರದೆವರುಕಾತೇನವತ್ಯು ಯಬಳಗೆಸಂದಯಮತವಯ್ಯಚಿ^14ಕಜೆಟಮಣ್ಣಿ ಹರುವವಡೀಗಳತುರಮುಡಿಕಾಫ್ ನದೇವಮನುಮಹಿಸನ^15ಹೊಮ್ಯುನಿನಿಸಿದನಸನಕಲಮಂಗಳಮಹಾಸ್ರಿ ಶ್ರಿ ಶ್ರಿ ಮಾದಯ್ಯನ^16ಪುಲುವನಸಿಪಸಹಜವಿನಸಹಜವಗವರಿದನುಮಂತಬಳಿಕೆಕನಿಸಿವಸಿ^17ಮಡಿನಿನಿಸಿದಸನಗಲಹಿಸಿಕೊಡಮಕ್ಷ ಳಕಲುದವೇದವಾಳಿಕೆಗಮನನಬತ^18ವೆಂಕುಜಾವದರೆಇಕಳಕಲಿದುಕುಹೂನುಸನಗಲಿಗೆಹೆಃ .ದಹಟುಜನಮಹಾಸನಕೋ^19ಜಮಮುತನ್ಯ ಜೊನೆಳಗೆಸಲುಪವಡೆಯುಸಃಕಿಯುತತೆಹೊನಪೂತ್ಹು || ಮಗಸಕೊಜ್ಞ^20ಚಿಕೊಡಿಯುನುದನೆಯ್ಕತ್ತೆ ತ್ತಿ ದ್ಧಿ ನುತನವದಿಡಗೆಸಕ್ಷಿ ಅದೆವಲ್ಕೇಕಳು^21ಕೇತರಪಳಯಉಯಿಗಮಉಡಜನವಮರ್ಕಳಿಗೆಉಪಬೆಟ್ಟು. ಹಣ್ಣಿಯನುಮಕಿ ದೇವಮನಗರಾಮು.^22ಚೇಜೆವಕೋಳಳದೇವವನಗರಕೋಡಿನವಡಮತಿದೇವವನಮಸುಂಜೇದೆ[ಪೋರೆಣೇಕ್ಕ ನಸೇನಜೋವ^23ವಮಧುಮ್ಮನಸುದಾಯಯನಕನಸಿಯಿಸಿಸಗರಬೆರುದ

cells.location: _At the same village, on a stone at the Bāṇêśvara temple._
cells.remarks: While vira-Ballâla-Dêva's son vira-Narasiṁga-Dêva was ruling the kingdom of the world :—in the year Pramâdi, Mâchi-Dêva, son of Immaḍi Dêvaṁvata-Râya, the great lord of Nugu-nâd and others (named) having entered into the temple, the priests who were joint managers, with the approval of all the *gaudas*, struck ? two blows (on the wall), and Mîdavâde of Belatûr, with the approval of the *gaudas* and elders of Nugu-nâd, caused the temple to be ? beautifully made (or rebuilt), at an expense of 60 *gadyāṇa* in cash, together with 470 *salige* of rice to the stone-masons. In the year Plavaṅga (? 1247 A.D.) on Mâdavâde's sons, Baṅkoḍe, Indâde, and Chekoḍe, these three, giving 13 *gadyāṇa* for plastering (the temple of) Bâṇêśvara, Belakalave gave 17 *gadyāṇa* for .. .. bricks, timber and mortar. Inabâde, he and the priests who are joint managers, will defray ? the charges. Some others (named) gave for the same god 4 *gadyāṇa*. (Usual final verse). This work of merit was carried out by Masanaya, son of Davôja, son of Kaḍalekere Kôve. In the year Târaṇa (? 1284 A.D.) at the *dîpâvali*, Helamâri-Vôdeya's son Naranâde, gave the cow which he had received for his share, as a tribute ..... drank the water of the sword (? an ordeal). Some others (named) gave two cows .......

year Pramâdi, Mâchi-Dêva, son of Immaḍi Dêvaṁvata-Râya, the great lord of Nugu-nâd and others
(named) having entered into the temple, the priests who were joint managers, with the approval of
all the *gaudas*, struck ? two blows (on the wall), and Mîdavâde of Belatûr, with the approval of the
*gaudas* and elders of Nugu-nâd, caused the temple to be ? beautifully made (or rebuilt), at an expense
of 60 *gadyāṇa* in cash, together with 470 *salige* of rice to the stone-masons.

In the year Plavaṅga (? 1247 A.D.) on Mâdavâde's sons, Baṅkoḍe, Indâde, and Chekoḍe, these
three, giving 13 *gadyāṇa* for plastering (the temple of) Bâṇêśvara, Belakalave gave 17 *gadyāṇa* for ..
.. bricks, timber and mortar. Inabâde, he and the priests who are joint managers, will defray ? the
charges. Some others (named) gave for the same god 4 *gadyāṇa*. (Usual final verse). This work
of merit was carried out by Masanaya, son of Davôja, son of Kaḍalekere Kôve.

In the year Târaṇa (? 1284 A.D.) at the *dîpâvali*, Helamâri-Vôdeya's son Naranâde, gave the
cow which he had received for his share, as a tribute ..... drank the water of the sword (? an
ordeal). Some others (named) gave two cows .......Read more (1 KB)

text.text_original: ಅದೇ ಗ್ರಾಮದ ಬಾಣೆಪ್ಪರಗುಡಿಯ ಬಳಿ ನೆಟ್ಟು  ್ಗನೆ ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ.ಪ್ರಮಾಣ 3’ 9” x 1’ 9”.[^1]ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಶ್ರೀವೀರುಳಲ್ಲಾ ಅಂದೆ[ವ್ರ]ನಮಗವೀಳನ[ರ]ಸಿಂಗದೇವಪ್ಪೃತ್ಥಿವೀರಾಜ್ಯೇ[^2]ತತ್ ಇರಲ್ವ್ರುವಾದಿಸಂವತ್ಸರದಲಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಶ್ರೀರಸುಗಾನಾದಮಹಾಪಾ[^3]ರ್ಭುಜವ್ಯ ದೀಪೇವಪವಕಾರಾಯನೆಮಗವಿತೆದೇವಕೋಲುಯದ[^4]ಉದ್ದಿ ಬೆಲೆಯುದಹಣ್ಬಿಲ್ಲುಯಂತುಕಂಜಿಯಾವಂಗಮುಜೆದೇವಿದುಲ್ಪೊ[^5]ನಹಳ್ಳಿ ಯವುಣೀಜೆಯುಂಹಕ್ಯ ರಘವುಮಜೆಯು[^6]ನಾಗುನಾಜದಮಹಪ್ರಭುಗಳುದುಚೆಪವಲ್ಯ್ಬೆಹಿಗೊಯಿಸಿದರ[^7]ಹುದುವಾಳಿಶೆಯತ್ನನ್ಸಿನಿಗಳ್ದುಲಡುತ್ತಿನೀಕ್ಕ ತಕ್ಕುಟುಬಿಡಿದರು[^8]ಪುಳತೂರವರದವಾಚೆಸನುಗನಾಧಉಲುಪಗಳುದಪುಳವರು[^9]ಲ್ಪುವನವಾದಿನುಟುಬಿನೆನೆಸಿನಾಡೇದವೆವಲಖ್ಯೆರಾಕೆಡಹೊನ್ನು ಗದೆಪ್ಪಿ[^10]ಣ ೨೦ ಕಾಳುಕಟಿಗಿಗರಕಾಣುಬೆತ್ವ ನ ೨೦ o ೨೦ ||[^11]ಪಲವಾಣಗಸಂವತರದಲುವಹದವಜೇಯುಮಕ್ತ ಕಂಬುಕಾಸಿ[^12]ಇಂದವಬೀಜೇಕಾಂತೆಂತ್ರೆಮೂರುನೋಲಗುಣರಾದೆವಾರಾಣಾಕ್ಷೆಗಡೆ[^13]ದೆಪ್ಪೆಹೊನಾಗ ೧೫ || ವಳಕಳವೆದುರುವರೇಕಾತ್ಯ್ಬೆಗಸುರವೆಸ[^14]ಸೂನ್ನು ಕೊಲುಗ ೧೧ || ಇನುವದೆಜೆಯಾತವಹುಮಾವಳಿಯುತಮತಿ[^15]ಗ೯ಳಾತ್ಮಫುಹಾಸುವರು || ನಾರಣಣೇವವರುಪಳತೇತನದಿವಿನಯು[^16]ಕ್ಕೆಷಾಕ್ಕಯುನುಅಜ್ಜುದ್ವಂದೇವಲ್ಪುಗಂಗದೇವ್ೃ ೨೧. ಸ್ವಸ್ತ್ಯಂವರನತ್ಯಂಹಗ್ಗ ದೇವನಕೋಟೆ ತಾಲೂಕು. 19117ಬಲಕೆರೆಜಕಸುಲಿಸಂಸ್ಥೆಯು | ವರಿಸನಹಸ್ಸಂಜಿಸಿಷ್ಠುಯುತ್ತೆಕಿನಿ ||18ಇದಮವಮಸಿದದಕಡಳೆಕೆಜೆಯುಕಾರವಱಜೂಜೇಶನುನಮಗ19ದೊಜಜಿನವಗನಮಸನೆಯು || ತರಣಸಂವತ್ಸರ ದವಿಸ, ಗಹೆಡಿಯು20ದವಷೆಯುಮಗನರನಳಕೇವವನುಗಗ21ದಳೆಗೋಷಹತಪಕವಲೆಕಥವಡೇತುಡುಂ22ಜಳೆಳುಯರುಬಗಲಂಗರಂಕುಡಿದರಸಣ್ತ23ದೇವಲುಬಲಕೆಜೇಗಡನಮಗದರೇಶಲ24ದೇವನವಗನುದೇವಮರಹಯುಕತವಮು25ಗಡಿಯುಬಲಕ್ಯೆಹಕೆಯಾರಮದೇವ. ತತೂ26ಹೋಸಕಲಾಯುಧವರಮದೇವಣಕಸತ27ತಜಮವಿಜೆಯುಪಂತಿವರುಬರುದವನಡೆ28ಗೋಷು, . ಹೇಕವಿಲೆ . . . ರತತಜುಜಿಸ29ರಲು

cells.remarks: While Muḍigoṇḍa-Râjēndra-Chôḷa was ruling the kingdom, in the 9th year of his reign, Oreya (or ? the chief) of Nugu-nâd, causing the ruined temple of Belatûr, which was broken down, and fallen level with the ground, to be rebuilt, and setting up the Liṅga which had been pulled out, Muruṅga-Seṭṭi's son Basavayya performed the Rudra-hōma, gave a feast to a thousand people, and casting forth the *bali*, completed the work of merit. And Jayamgoṇḍa-Chôḷa-Permaḍi-Gâvuṇḍa, son of Javani-Gâvuṇḍa of Belatûr, and Basava-Seṭṭi, the good son born to Maruga-Seṭṭi and Mâggabbe of the same place, paying the money and acquiring the land, presented for the temple, with the knowledge of the village and the five ? chief men 15 ploughs of wet land and 5 ploughs of flower garden. And Basava-Seṭṭi also gave land for a perpetual lamp ?, (its boundaries). Chôvavu, the ? representative of Basava-Seṭṭi, caused this to be written. 68 Heggadadēvankōte Taluq.

cells.location: *At the same village, on a stone near the Binakalammi temple in Aidakatte-hoḷa.*
cells.remarks: Be it well. The Chōla-Rāja having captured the whole world, Rājēndra-Dēva, celebrated as the destroyer of the hosts of his wicked enemies; it being the 6th year (of his reign), and moreover in detail, according to the S'aka era, the year 979, known as Hēmalambi, the auspicious month Kārttika, the 12th of the dark fortnight, Monday :— Be it well. Praised by all the world, reckoned the chief of the Avacharas, of exalted merit, established in the highest valour, warriors, donors and guardians, were the rulers of Nugu-nād; in whose line was born the matchless Ereyanga. His son was Echa, equal to Manu. To him was born a son Javaniyamna, the abode of intelligence. To that Javanayya and to the ornament of women Jākabbe, bringing good fortune, was born, a thunderbolt weapon to the mountains hostile kings, Raviga. Along with Raviga was born wisdom, along with wisdom was born wealth, and along with wealth was born generosity, what greater than these could there be? Favourite of the farmers, an ornament of farmers, the Rāma of Nugu-nād, a Karna of the Kali age, the abode of happiness, generosity and valour,—can he be compared with the base, worthless, evil, unrighteous, uncivilised, and ignorant of the present day—this worthy chief of the Avacharas? On inquiring at the courts of the Chōla, Pallava, S'ilāmēgha, Kērala, Sōrata, Gāreva, Bhōja, Lāla, Gajapati, Hayapati, and Narapati kings, he alone is the fit subject for praise by dancers, bards and minstrels, the ornament of chiefs, Jayamgonda-Chōla-Per-mānadi-Gāvunda. On the Chōla king presenting him with a spreading umbrella, a conch, cymbals, and royal elephant, the favourite of farmers acquired the rank of a mandalika: to the shores of the ocean, to the limits of the universe, to the tusks of the elephants at the points of the compass, did the vine of the fame spread of the favourite of farmers. To the ruler of Ede-nād, the equal of Manu, a mine of refinement, true of speech, the chief Nāl- gōja, by his wife Bhūtabbe, was born the jewel of women, known as the Sitā of the Kali age, Ponnak- abbe; whom the ruler of Belatūr, the equal of Manu, took in marriage; his celebrated wife, can she be compared with the wives of the world? In matchless virtue, in disposition, in high generosity, in spiritual devotion, the equal of the Mountain-daughter (Pārvati), Rambhe, Mēnake, Sarasvati, Ruk- mini, Satyabhāme, can the pure-minded Ponnakabbe be compared with those of the present day—wicked, worthless, badly disposed, ill-mannered and low? Heggadadcvankotc Taluq. 69 To the virtuous, the refined, the purifier of her gotra, the well mannered, the jewel of women, Ponnabbe, and to Raviga, was born Dekabbe, who was given in marriage to Echa of Pervvayal, the ruler of Navale-nad, of the Kuruvanda family, and he lived happily with that lotus-eyed one, a jewel of modesty, devoted to her husband. While, famous as a wrestler, a mill in pounding his enemies, he was thus living happily, having thrown and in the crush killed his kinsmen, the king had him taken off straight to Talekad and put to death. On hearing the report that they had put to death the Vela of the Kali age, brave and gene- rous,—that beautiful one, the light of Raviga's family, went forth to the fire-pit to die. Her father and mother together, and all her relations, coming, besought her, saying, " Daughter, do not die,"—and all falling down, embraced her feet. But the innocent Dekabbe, becoming angry, exclaiming said, " Being praised as the daughter of Raviga, the ruler of Nugu-nad, and the wife of the ruler of Navale-nad, can I have any mind to live, and disgrace the good name of his house who gave me (in marriage) and of his who took me (in marriage) ?" Having thus made her decision, she presented to the god a garden to provide for a perpetual lamp, and saying it was for the offerings, that lotus-eyed one, with reverence, also presented certain other land (described). On all united again and again saying, " Don't (do it): stop,"—she said, " Be silent: I will not stop," and with kindly words giving away (her) land, gold-embroidered cloths, cows and money, and folding her hands with love to the god of gods, she entered the blazing flames, Dekabbe, and winning the approval of all the world and the daily celebration of her praises, went to the world of gods. The beautiful S'ri, Gauri, S'achi, the daughter of the earth (Sita), Rati, the beautiful Earth (goddess), the embodiment of beauty, intelligence, goodness and generosity, crowned with victory, fame,— principle and reverence, devoted to her husband, firm and energetic, this celebrated mine of heroism, this ocean of constancy, this treasury of good qualities, the famous Dekale, this jewel of womankind, who can forget in the whole world? who is she that is superior to this best of women? The refuge of the learned, the Raghava of Nugu-nad, a lion to the wrathful, liberator of..... great in valour, the favourite of farmers, the Karnna of the Kali age, champion over the envious, a wishing-stone to bards, his head at the feet of S'iva, from affection for his daughter, as a memorial to all the world, erected this stone monument. The land which Dekabbe left to Mahadeva, the piece of garden land and the five kolagas of rice- land to the south of the Malte tank she had created, may those born in this family protect and do her honour. Those who do not fulfill this will have their portion in hell. The friend of poets who use not words in vain, Malla,—son of him of the Marupas, distinguished among Brahmans as without spot and without concealment, Aditya, the famous conveyor of intelli- gence,—wrote this. The achari who was a lion to the wrathful and a champion over the envious engraved it.

text.remarks:
Be it well. The Chōla-Rāja having captured the whole world, Rājēndra-Dēva, celebrated as the
destroyer of the hosts of his wicked enemies; it being the 6th year (of his reign), and moreover in
detail, according to the S'aka era, the year 979, known as Hēmalambi, the auspicious month Kārttika,
the 12th of the dark fortnight, Monday :—

Be it well. Praised by all the world, reckoned the chief of the Avacharas, of exalted merit,
established in the highest valour, warriors, donors and guardians, were the rulers of Nugu-nād; in
whose line was born the matchless Ereyanga. His son was Echa, equal to Manu. To him was born
a son Javaniyamna, the abode of intelligence. To that Javanayya and to the ornament of women
Jākabbe, bringing good fortune, was born, a thunderbolt weapon to the mountains hostile kings, Raviga.
Along with Raviga was born wisdom, along with wisdom was born wealth, and along with wealth was
born generosity, what greater than these could there be? Favourite of the farmers, an ornament of
farmers, the Rāma of Nugu-nād, a Karna of the Kali age, the abode of happiness, generosity and
valour,—can he be compared with the base, worthless, evil, unrighteous, uncivilised, and ignorant of
the present day—this worthy chief of the Avacharas?

On inquiring at the courts of the Chōla, Pallava, S'ilāmēgha, Kērala, Sōrata, Gāreva, Bhōja, Lāla,
Gajapati, Hayapati, and Narapati kings, he alone is the fit subject for praise by dancers, bards and
minstrels, the ornament of chiefs, Jayamgonda-Chōla-Per-mānadi-Gāvunda.

On the Chōla king presenting him with a spreading umbrella, a conch, cymbals, and royal
elephant, the favourite of farmers acquired the rank of a mandalika: to the shores of the ocean,
to the limits of the universe, to the tusks of the elephants at the points of the compass, did the vine
of the fame spread of the favourite of farmers.

To the ruler of Ede-nād, the equal of Manu, a mine of refinement, true of speech, the chief Nāl-
gōja, by his wife Bhūtabbe, was born the jewel of women, known as the Sitā of the Kali age, Ponnak-
abbe; whom the ruler of Belatūr, the equal of Manu, took in marriage; his celebrated wife, can she be
compared with the wives of the world? In matchless virtue, in disposition, in high generosity, in
spiritual devotion, the equal of the Mountain-daughter (Pārvati), Rambhe, Mēnake, Sarasvati, Ruk-
mini, Satyabhāme, can the pure-minded Ponnakabbe be compared with those of the present day—wicked,
worthless, badly disposed, ill-mannered and low?

Heggadadcvankotc Taluq. 69
To the virtuous, the refined, the purifier of her gotra, the well mannered, the jewel of women,
Ponnabbe, and to Raviga, was born Dekabbe, who was given in marriage to Echa of Pervvayal, the ruler
of Navale-nad, of the Kuruvanda family, and he lived happily with that lotus-eyed one, a jewel of
modesty, devoted to her husband.

While, famous as a wrestler, a mill in pounding his enemies, he was thus living happily, having
thrown and in the crush killed his kinsmen, the king had him taken off straight to Talekad and put
to death. On hearing the report that they had put to death the Vela of the Kali age, brave and gene-
rous,—that beautiful one, the light of Raviga's family, went forth to the fire-pit to die.

Her father and mother together, and all her relations, coming, besought her, saying, " Daughter,
do not die,"—and all falling down, embraced her feet. But the innocent Dekabbe, becoming angry,
exclaiming said, " Being praised as the daughter of Raviga, the ruler of Nugu-nad, and the wife of the
ruler of Navale-nad, can I have any mind to live, and disgrace the good name of his house who gave
me (in marriage) and of his who took me (in marriage) ?"

Having thus made her decision, she presented to the god a garden to provide for a perpetual
lamp, and saying it was for the offerings, that lotus-eyed one, with reverence, also presented certain
other land (described).

On all united again and again saying, " Don't (do it): stop,"—she said, " Be silent: I will not
stop," and with kindly words giving away (her) land, gold-embroidered cloths, cows and money, and
folding her hands with love to the god of gods, she entered the blazing flames, Dekabbe, and winning
the approval of all the world and the daily celebration of her praises, went to the world of gods.

The beautiful S'ri, Gauri, S'achi, the daughter of the earth (Sita), Rati, the beautiful Earth
(goddess), the embodiment of beauty, intelligence, goodness and generosity, crowned with victory, fame,—
principle and reverence, devoted to her husband, firm and energetic, this celebrated mine of heroism,
this ocean of constancy, this treasury of good qualities, the famous Dekale, this jewel of womankind,
who can forget in the whole world? who is she that is superior to this best of women?

The refuge of the learned, the Raghava of Nugu-nad, a lion to the wrathful, liberator of.....
great in valour, the favourite of farmers, the Karnna of the Kali age, champion over the envious, a
wishing-stone to bards, his head at the feet of S'iva, from affection for his daughter, as a memorial to
all the world, erected this stone monument.

The land which Dekabbe left to Mahadeva, the piece of garden land and the five kolagas of rice-
land to the south of the Malte tank she had created, may those born in this family protect and do her
honour. Those who do not fulfill this will have their portion in hell.

The friend of poets who use not words in vain, Malla,—son of him of the Marupas, distinguished
among Brahmans as without spot and without concealment, Aditya, the famous conveyor of intelli-
gence,—wrote this.

text.location: At Kallambālu (Saraguru hobli), on a stone in front of the Kāmēśvara temple.
text.remarks:
Inseparable as a word and its meaning, the parents of the world, Pârvati and Paramêsvara do
I reverence, that I may receive both words and sense.1

The temple of the god Kâmêsvara in the village of Kalambâl, otherwise called Silepura, having
fallen to ruin, Kappanna-Gauḍa, son of Sambu-Gauḍa, son of Kannappa-Linge-Gauḍa of the Kalla-
hali-kula, had it repaired with strong supports at the eight points of the compass. (Usual benediction).
Obeisance to S'ambhu and Sadâsiva.

Heggadadevankote Taluq.                         71

cells.location: On a second stone in front of the same temple. [→ At Kallambālu (Saraguru hobli), on a stone in front of the Kāmēśvara temple.]
cells.remarks: While (with usual titles) the pratāpa-chakravartti Hoysana-vīra-Ballāla-Dēva was ruling the kingdom of the world in peace and wisdom :—Mañchayya-Danṇāyaka, younger brother of the great minister and sarvvādhikāri, of the Bhāradvāja-gōtra, the senior danḍanāyaka Gōvindamayya, and all the chiefs and farmers of the Fourteen-nāḍs, together with Nugu-nāḍ Oṇka-Gauḍa of the .. macha family, Voddi-Gauḍa, the ruler of Immadi-nāḍ, and all the citizens of Kallambāḷa, made a grant of Kundanūr in Nugu-nāḍ, to provide for the daily offerings and other ceremonies of the god Kaliyuga- Kāmēsvara of Kallambāḷa.

svasti samasta-bhuvanāśrayam śrī-pṛithvi-vallabham mahārājādhirājam paramēśvaram Dvāravatī-pura-

Ādivāra-Puṣhya-nakshatra-Śiva-yōga-Balava-karaṇad andu Bharadvāja-gōtrada svasti śrīman-mahā-
pradhānaṁ sarvvādhikāri hiriya-dauḍanāyaka Gōvindamayyaṅgala tamma Mañchayya-Daṇṇāyakaruṁ
Haḍinālku-nāḍa samasta-prabhu-gauṁdugalum Nugu-nāda . macha-vaṁsadā Oṅka-Gauḍa Yimmadi-
nād-ālva Voddi-Gauḍa Kallambāla-samasta-nakharāṅgalu mukhyav āgi Nugu-nād-olagana Kuṇḍūranu

ಅದೇ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನದ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಕಡೆ ನೆಟ್ಟು ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ.
ಪ್ರಮಾಣ 5' 6″ x 1' 9″.
^1ನವಮಸ್ತು ^2ಗಾರಗಸನ್ನಿ ೧ಂಸಕದೃಬಾ ಮರತರ^
^3ವೇತ್ರ್ಯುಳೋಕ್ಯನಗಾರಂಭಭೂಪಾಲಸ್ಯಬ್ಯಾಲಕುಳಧವೇೆ ||
^4ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸಮಸ್ತ ಭುವನಪ್ರಿಯಯಿಶ್ರೀಪ್ರಿಯವಲ್ಲಭಮಹಾರಾ
^5ಜಾಧಿರಾಜಪರಮೇಶ್ವರದವ್ಯಾರಾವೆತಪ್ರಭವರಾಧೀಪ್ತ
^6ರಾಯದೇವಕಾಲೆಯಂದಿಯ್ವಾನಿಸಮೇವತ್ಯಕೇಶವನಮತಿ
^7ರಾಜರಾಜಮುಲಿಸೆರೊಳಗಣ್ಣಗಣ್ಣಭೀರುಂಡಕಡನಪ್ರಚಂಡ
^8ನಿಸಂಕಪ್ರತಾಪಹಕ್ಕವತಿ. ^9ಶ್ರೀಹೇಮಸಾವಿರಬಳಲ್ಲಳದೆವರುಂ
ಶ್ರೀಮತ್ ^10ಬಿರುದಿನುಡಿಯನವಕೇತಲಮುಹಾದೇವಿರುಯಂಬುಸಿಂಹಫಾವಿ^
^11ನೋರಾದಿಪ್ರಿಸ್ಯಿಳೋಜನ್ಯಯೋತ್ಯಮಿಲ || ತಕುಮಾದವದವೇದಪ^
^12ಜೀವಿಮುಪ್ಪಸ್ತ್ರಿಶ್ರಿಮನುಮಹಾಪ್ಯಧಾನಸಂವಾಪಧಿಕಾರಿ^
^13ಮಹಾಪ್ರಸಾದ್ವಯ್ಯಲುಬಹತ್ತ ರಡಿಯೋಂಗಾಧಿಪತಿಯು^
^14ನೇದುಪಕಳೇಣಾಧಿರಾಜ್ಯಪುತ್ರ ರಾಯಸನಗಾಂಗತವ^
^15ಜಪಹಜಕರದೇವರಂಗಸಖಬ್ಯಾಕರಸೋಸಹಭೂಮ್ಯಂ^
^16ನೆನುಮತೇಟಿಕಾಲಯಾಂಡ್ಯಾತ್ರೇಜಿನಕಳವ್ಯಿವಿರಧವಾರಣಾಸಿ^
^17ಹೋರೋದರಸತ್ಯಾರಾಭ್ಯಯುಪ್ಪಪ್ರಧಾನಕಳಕಳಭುಯಧರನಾ
^18ಫಕ್ರೀಯಮುತ್ಪತಿಲಿಂಗಸ್ವಕೇದಾರದೇವಳ ^19ಮೂದಾರಾ
^20ಧಕಂಕರಬಳಳಸಘಕರವಸ್ಸು ಕಮಾರಮಾವಧವದಣ್ಣ^\
^21ಯಾಕರೂಂಕರಳಿವದವಂಕಾ ಯುಕರಂಕುಮಾರನಪಕಾಧಿಪ್ರಿ^
^22ತಮವಾಂಗುಸಿಬಿನಾಳತ್ತು ಮಿಧ್ಯುಶ್ಕಕವರ್ಷದ ೧೪೨೯ನೆಯ^
^23ಯುಕಾರ್ಷದಸಂವತ್ಸರದವರೂಷದಪುಣ್ಣಮಿಲಿದವಾರಅ^
^24 ಳ್ಳಿ ಈನಕ್ಷತ್ರ ಅಉಯ್ಯಾಂಸರಿಯೋಗೆ ಬವಕರಣಸೋಮ^
^25ಗೆಗ್ರಹೊಂದರದುನಗನಾವಾಕಸ್ಕಳಬಳನಗರದಪುಣ್ಯತೀರ್ತ್ಥ ರಾನುಗ^
^26ವಿನವುತ್ಥ ರೇಲಿಶರವದಯ್ಯ ಕಾಮಮ್ಮಕ್ಕರದೇವರಲಗಭೋಗೇರಂಗಂ
ಭೋಗೇ
^27ಕ್ಯ್ ನುಗುನಾಯಿಕಳಿಗಣಿಕುಂಜೋರನಶ್ರೀಕಳುವಾರಮಾವಧವ^
^28ದಂಗಾಣ್ಯ ಯುಕರೂಂದಿನಲ್ಲಾ ನಿಸಹನಸವ್ಯ ಪ್ರಭುಗಾಉಂ^
^29ಹುಗಂಳಸಬ್ಭ್ಯಾಕಳಭುಧಪಹರವಗಾಂವದೃಶ್ಯತಾ^
^30ರಂಬರಸಂಲುವಂತಭಾಗಿದಾರಾಪ್ಪುಣ್ಯಕಾಪಮಾಡಿಕೊ^
^31 ಟ್ಟವದತ್ತಿ || ಕಾಲುಬಳಿಯಮಂಡಲಸ್ಥಾನಮಿನಬಿರಂಗಳಬುಟ್ಟ್ಯ
^32ಕೌಯುಮತ್ತ ರೆಂದು || ಬಹುಭಿಷವಸುಧಾಸುಧಾಭುಕ್ಕೋ ೇರಾ^
^33ಬೂಭಿ ಸಿರದಾರೀಬಿರ್ಯಸ್ಯುಸ್ಸ್ಯಾಯುಧಾಭೂಮಿಮಿತಸ್ಯ್
^34ತಸ್ಯತದಫಲಂ || ಸ್ವದತ್ತಾ ಾಯರದತ್ತಾ ವಾಯೋರೇಹರೇ
^35ತಿವನುಧಂರಾಪಾಷ್ಯೈವ್ಯ್ಕಳಿಹಸ ಸಹಸ್ರಪ್ರೀಲಿವಪ್ಯ
^36ಯಾಜಾಯುತತ್ರಿಮಿ ||

text.text_original: ಅದೇ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನದ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಕಡೆ ನೆಟ್ಟು ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ.ಪ್ರಮಾಣ 5' 6″ x 1' 9″.^1ನವಮಸ್ತು ^2ಗಾರಗಸನ್ನಿ ೧ಂಸಕದೃಬಾ ಮರತರ^^3ವೇತ್ರ್ಯುಳೋಕ್ಯನಗಾರಂಭಭೂಪಾಲಸ್ಯಬ್ಯಾಲಕುಳಧವೇೆ ||^4ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸಮಸ್ತ ಭುವನಪ್ರಿಯಯಿಶ್ರೀಪ್ರಿಯವಲ್ಲಭಮಹಾರಾ^5ಜಾಧಿರಾಜಪರಮೇಶ್ವರದವ್ಯಾರಾವೆತಪ್ರಭವರಾಧೀಪ್ತ^6ರಾಯದೇವಕಾಲೆಯಂದಿಯ್ವಾನಿಸಮೇವತ್ಯಕೇಶವನಮತಿ^7ರಾಜರಾಜಮುಲಿಸೆರೊಳಗಣ್ಣಗಣ್ಣಭೀರುಂಡಕಡನಪ್ರಚಂಡ^8ನಿಸಂಕಪ್ರತಾಪಹಕ್ಕವತಿ. ^9ಶ್ರೀಹೇಮಸಾವಿರಬಳಲ್ಲಳದೆವರುಂಶ್ರೀಮತ್ ^10ಬಿರುದಿನುಡಿಯನವಕೇತಲಮುಹಾದೇವಿರುಯಂಬುಸಿಂಹಫಾವಿ^^11ನೋರಾದಿಪ್ರಿಸ್ಯಿಳೋಜನ್ಯಯೋತ್ಯಮಿಲ || ತಕುಮಾದವದವೇದಪ^^12ಜೀವಿಮುಪ್ಪಸ್ತ್ರಿಶ್ರಿಮನುಮಹಾಪ್ಯಧಾನಸಂವಾಪಧಿಕಾರಿ^^13ಮಹಾಪ್ರಸಾದ್ವಯ್ಯಲುಬಹತ್ತ ರಡಿಯೋಂಗಾಧಿಪತಿಯು^^14ನೇದುಪಕಳೇಣಾಧಿರಾಜ್ಯಪುತ್ರ ರಾಯಸನಗಾಂಗತವ^^15ಜಪಹಜಕರದೇವರಂಗಸಖಬ್ಯಾಕರಸೋಸಹಭೂಮ್ಯಂ^^16ನೆನುಮತೇಟಿಕಾಲಯಾಂಡ್ಯಾತ್ರೇಜಿನಕಳವ್ಯಿವಿರಧವಾರಣಾಸಿ^^17ಹೋರೋದರಸತ್ಯಾರಾಭ್ಯಯುಪ್ಪಪ್ರಧಾನಕಳಕಳಭುಯಧರನಾ^18ಫಕ್ರೀಯಮುತ್ಪತಿಲಿಂಗಸ್ವಕೇದಾರದೇವಳ ^19ಮೂದಾರಾ^20ಧಕಂಕರಬಳಳಸಘಕರವಸ್ಸು ಕಮಾರಮಾವಧವದಣ್ಣ^\^21ಯಾಕರೂಂಕರಳಿವದವಂಕಾ ಯುಕರಂಕುಮಾರನಪಕಾಧಿಪ್ರಿ^^22ತಮವಾಂಗುಸಿಬಿನಾಳತ್ತು ಮಿಧ್ಯುಶ್ಕಕವರ್ಷದ ೧೪೨೯ನೆಯ^^23ಯುಕಾರ್ಷದಸಂವತ್ಸರದವರೂಷದಪುಣ್ಣಮಿಲಿದವಾರಅ^^24 ಳ್ಳಿ ಈನಕ್ಷತ್ರ ಅಉಯ್ಯಾಂಸರಿಯೋಗೆ ಬವಕರಣಸೋಮ^^25ಗೆಗ್ರಹೊಂದರದುನಗನಾವಾಕಸ್ಕಳಬಳನಗರದಪುಣ್ಯತೀರ್ತ್ಥ ರಾನುಗ^^26ವಿನವುತ್ಥ ರೇಲಿಶರವದಯ್ಯ ಕಾಮಮ್ಮಕ್ಕರದೇವರಲಗಭೋಗೇರಂಗಂಭೋಗೇ^27ಕ್ಯ್ ನುಗುನಾಯಿಕಳಿಗಣಿಕುಂಜೋರನಶ್ರೀಕಳುವಾರಮಾವಧವ^^28ದಂಗಾಣ್ಯ ಯುಕರೂಂದಿನಲ್ಲಾ ನಿಸಹನಸವ್ಯ ಪ್ರಭುಗಾಉಂ^^29ಹುಗಂಳಸಬ್ಭ್ಯಾಕಳಭುಧಪಹರವಗಾಂವದೃಶ್ಯತಾ^^30ರಂಬರಸಂಲುವಂತಭಾಗಿದಾರಾಪ್ಪುಣ್ಯಕಾಪಮಾಡಿಕೊ^^31 ಟ್ಟವದತ್ತಿ || ಕಾಲುಬಳಿಯಮಂಡಲಸ್ಥಾನಮಿನಬಿರಂಗಳಬುಟ್ಟ್ಯ^32ಕೌಯುಮತ್ತ ರೆಂದು || ಬಹುಭಿಷವಸುಧಾಸುಧಾಭುಕ್ಕೋ ೇರಾ^^33ಬೂಭಿ ಸಿರದಾರೀಬಿರ್ಯಸ್ಯುಸ್ಸ್ಯಾಯುಧಾಭೂಮಿಮಿತಸ್ಯ್^34ತಸ್ಯತದಫಲಂ || ಸ್ವದತ್ತಾ ಾಯರದತ್ತಾ ವಾಯೋರೇಹರೇ^35ತಿವನುಧಂರಾಪಾಷ್ಯೈವ್ಯ್ಕಳಿಹಸ ಸಹಸ್ರಪ್ರೀಲಿವಪ್ಯ^36ಯಾಜಾಯುತತ್ರಿಮಿ ||

cells.location: *At Naḷḷūru, (Saraguru hobli) on a stone to the east of the Virabhadra temple.*
cells.remarks: .... Nāyaka, agent for the affairs of Mādhavayya, chief at the court of Achyuta-Dēva-mahārāya, made a grant of the village of Nallūr in Baya-nāḍ to Vodeyar of Hura in Kōṭe-śīme, together with all the eight rights (named, as usual) of full possession, to be enjoyed by him, his sons grand- sons and descendants, as long as sun moon endure.
cells.text_roman:
Svasti śrī vijayābhyudaya S'ālivāhana-saka-varusha 1452 sandu Khara-samvatsarada . . . . . .
Achyuta-Dēva-mahārāyaru . . . . . . . . . . . . . . āsthānad odeya Mādhavayyanavara kāryyake karttar ada . .
. . . . Nāyakaru Kōteya-simeya Hurada . . . . . . . vodeyarige sarvvamānyav āgi koṭṭa Bāya-nāda valaga
Naḷḷūra-grāmada chatu-simey-olagada akshiṇi-āgāmi-nidhi-nikshēpa-jala-pāshāṇa-siddha-sādhyagal
emba ashṭa-bhōga-tējas-sāmya-volagagi kotev āgi nīvu nimma putra-pautra-paramparey āgi a-chandrarkka-sthāyigal āgi sukadali anubhavisi-koṇḍu bahiri yeṁdu koṭṭa śila-sāsana (usual final verse)
cells.text_original:
ಅದೇ ಹೋಬಳಿ ಬೇಚೀರಾಂ ನಲ್ಲೂರು ಗ್ರಾಮದ ವೀರಭದ್ರ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನಕ್ಕೆ ಪೂರ್ವದಲ್ಲಿ ನೆಟ್ಟ ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ.
ಪ್ರಮಾಣ 3' 6" x 3'.
^1ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಶ್ರೀ[i]ವಿಜಯಾಭ್ಯುದಯಶಾಲಿವಾಹನಶಕವರುಷ
^2೧೫೪೦ ನೆಯ . . . ವಾದವಿರಸಂತತ್ತರದ
3 . . . . ರದೆಉಳಿತುತದೇವಮಹಾರಾಯರು
4 . . . . . ಅಸ್ಗ್ಯನದೊಡೆಸುಮಾಧವಯವನರಕೆಯಕ್ಯೂ
^5ಶಕತರಾದ . . . . . ನಾಯಕರುಕಟ್ಟಿರಬೀಸಿನು
^6ಯುಪಾರದ . . . ವ್ಹಜೆಯರಾಗೆಸ್ವರ್ಣಮನ್ನಾವಾಗಿಕೊಟ್ಟು
^7ಬಯುವನಾಪಳಗಳಲ್ಟುರಾಗ್ರಾಮನಡತಹಸಿನೆಯುಳಾಗ
^8ದಕ್ಷಿಣೋಳಗಾಮವಿನಿನಿಷ್ಠೆಪ್ರಜಾಪಾಲಪಾಳಾನಿಧಿ ಸಾ
9ದ್ರ್ಗಗಳಂಬಲಸ್ಥ್ಯ ಭೂೇಳಗತೇಜಸಾಮಂವ್ಯವಹಾರಿಗಳ್ಕೋಟಿವಾಗಿ
10ಸೀಪುನಿಮ್ಮ ಪುತ್ರ ಪೋತ್ರಪರಂಪರಯಾಗಲಿಕಂ
11ವ್ರಾಕ್ಷ್ಮಣ್ಯ ಯುಗೀಗಾಣಿಸುಕದಲೆಅನುಭಿವಸಿಕೊಂಡುಬಟು
12ರಿಯಂಕುತುಕೊಟ್ಟಿಲಾಸಹಸ್ರದತ್ತ್ಪ ವರರದತ್ತ್ಪ ವೊ
13ಯೋಹರೇತಿವಸುಂಧರಾಪಷಿಂವ್ಹ್ಯರುಪುನಸ್ರ್ವಸ್ತೀನಿ
(ಮುಂದೆ ಬರವಣಿಗೆ ಇಲ್ಲ)

ಅದೇ ಹೋಬಳಿ ಮುಸಹಳ್ಳ್ಯ ಗ್ರಾಮದ ಗುರುಳುವಮಾರೀಗೂಡಿಯ ಮುಂದೆ ನೆಟ್ಟಿ ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ.
^1ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಶ್ರೀನಿಜಯಾಭ್ಯುದಯಶಾಲಿವಾಹನಶಕ
^2ವರುಷ ೧೫ಳೀ ಸನಚೇಸಂತವರುತ್ತರದೆಸಪ್ತವನುಷ
^3ಕಿ ಸುಕ್ಕವಾರದಉಳುಕ್ಕುಷ್ಠ ದೇವಮಹಾರುರಾಯರಾದ
^4ಶ್ರೀಮಭುಜನಾ ನರಪತಿಕೃಷ್ಣ ರಾಯರಾಯಸಾದರುಳಹೂ
^5ಕೊಯಲು.ಸೀಮೆಯವಹರುದನಾಥಪನಾಯಕರೆಗಳಿಗೆಪುವ್ಹ್ರಾ
^6ಸ್ವಸ್ತಮಿನಿಕೊಟ್ಟಿಬದ್ಯಣಾಜನ್ನ ಅಧವಮಸಿಹಳ್ಯ ಸುದಹಾ
^7ಲುವದೆದೇವರಾಯಸಪುರಾಯಗಾಮದವೊಳಾಗಾವಹತುಸ್ತಿನಮೆಯೂ
^8ಳಾಗದಶಕ್ಷಿಣೋಳಗಾಮವಿನಿಧಿಕ್ಷೇಜಲಪಾಪಾಳಾನಿಧಿ ಸರ್ವ್ಯ
^9ವೇಚೆಉಳಪವಿನೋಗೆತೇಜಸ್ವಾಮ್ಯವ್ಯವಹಾರಿಗಳ್ಕೋಟಿವಾಗಿನಿನೀಲು
^೧೦ತ್ರಾಪೋತ್ರಪರಂಪರಸಂತತಿಯಾಗಲೀಚೆಂದ್ರ್ಯಕ್ಕಾಸೆಟ್ಟ್ಯ ಯುಗೋಗಾಲು
ಕದಲಿ
^11ಅನುಭಿವಸಿಕೊಂಡುಬಿರಿಯಿಂದಮುಸಿಸಿನಿಲಿಯೋಲಾಪಕಾಹನೆ ||
ಗೃಹತ || ಯೋಕ್ಯೆ
^12ಪಭಗಿನೀಲೋಕೇಸೆನ್ಮಯೋಕ್ಯೆ ವಿಯೋಭೂಪಾನುಭೂಜಾ್ಯ
ಸಕರಾಣ್ಯಾದ್ರವ್ಯದತ್ಯಾವ
^13ಸುಂದರಾ || ಸ್ವದತ್ತಾಂಪರದತ್ತಾಂವಾಂವಾಯೋಹರೇತಾವಸುಂಧ
ರಾಲ್‌ಷಿತ್ವೇವಿಷ್ಪಪಸದಸುಸ್ರಾ
^14ನೀವಿಪ್ಯಾಂಜಾಯತೇಕೃಮಿ ||

cells.location: At Kōṭāgūḷa (Saraguru hobli), on a stone near the Māri temple.
cells.remarks: Muriyya-Râvu sent to Chennana-Setti, for the purpose of promoting intercourse and friendship, a message as follows,—You having, of your own consent, made a boundary for all the roads from Bhettakarli of Saragûr to Bhettakarli of Hura,—in the same manner, for the god Bhairava ? we have given certain lands (boundaries described), to continue as long as sun and moon.

cells.location: *At Narasipura (Nemmanahaḷḷi hobli), on a stone in the S'āsana-gudi.*

^9ಸನಾಧಿಕ್ಷರದಕಣ್ಠೀರವರನರಸರಾಜೋಜೆಯ

'1ಪ್ರಭುವಮಾಧವನಾಯಕರ್‌ಕವರುದಳವ
^12ಯಲಿಂಗಾರಜ್ಯೆಯನವರುನರಸಿಂಹಸ್ವಾಮಿ
^13ಯವರಅಲಂಗಾರಣ್ಯಭೋಗೇಅಮ್ಮತಪಡಿ
^14ತಟಾಕಗಣೇಚಿಯವಾರಧನಗೇಸೂರನಲಕ್ಕೆ
^15ಸಲುವನರಸೀಪುರವರದಗಮ್ಮ೧ ಕಕ್ಕೆಸಲುವ
^16ಚತಸೀಮೆಯಯಾescuಕಟ್ಟೆ ದಾನಸಾಸನ ।
^17ಸ್ವದತ್ತಾ ದ್ವಿ ಗುಣಂಪುಣ್ಯಂಪರದತ್ತಾ ನುಪಾ
^18ಲನಂಸದರದತ್ತಾ ತ್ಪಹಾರೇಣಸ್ವದತ್ತಂನಿಷ್ಪಲಂಭತ್
^19ಪೇತ್ರಪೃಥ್ವತ್ತಾ ವಪವರದತ್ತಾ ೪ನ್ಮಾವೋಯೇರೇವತಿಣಸುಂಧರಾ

cells.location: *At the same village, on a virakal in Javanē-Gauḍa's field.*
cells.remarks: While, with all titles, the mahâ-maṇḍalêśvara, boon lord of Dvârâvati-pura, Mukkanna-Kadam-ba (!)^1 was ruling the kingdom of . . . ba-nâd :—Bicha-Gavuḍa, son of Bamma-Gavuḍa of Heggavâḍi, Heggadadēvankōṭe Taluq. having recovered the cows, slew the robbers, ravishing the women, and died. On which Viranna set up this stone. (Verse in praise of Bicha). All the farmers of Kuṇḍatūr made a grant of a koḍaṅgi for Bicha. (Imprecation). Footnote 1. The titles and date belong to the Hoysala king Vishṇuvardhana.

text.text_original: ಅದೇ ಗ್ರಾಮಕ್ಕೆ ಪೂರ್ವ ಜವನೇಗೌಡನ ಹೊಲದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ವೀರಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ.ಪ್ರಮಾಣ 4′ 6″ × 4′ 4″.^1ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸವಸ್ತ^2ಪ್ರಸನ್ನ ಸ್ಯಟು^3ತತ್ತ್ರೀವಸ್ತೃ^4 ಹಾವಣ್ಣ ಅಲೆಯರ  ^5ದ್ವಾರವತೀಪ್ರು  ^6ಳವರಾಲಿಘ್ನ  ^7ರಮುಚಕಣ್ಮಕ  ^8ಹೌಬಿಟ್ಟೇ. . .  ^9ಬಿನಾಸರಜ್ಜೋ  ^10ಗಡಿಯು || . . .  ^11ಸಕವದಸಂ ೧೦೩೦ ಸಾಸಿರದ. . . ತೃ ನೆಯ್ಯು^12ಗಳನಂಮೊಳ್ಳಾಗಡಲ್ಲಿ.^13ವೆಪ್ಪೆರೆದವರ್ಗಗ್ಗಳಸರಸಂಕೆ^14ಮೋಣ್ಸುದ್ದುಪಿಕಾಬಸಿ ೧೧^15ಬ್ರಿಯೆಹಸ್ತಿನವರಮೂಹಗ್ಗೆ ವೇದಿಯು . . .    ರಟಮ್ಮಗಾಪ್ಪಣ^16ಪ್ಪಿಯುಪುತ್ರಬಳಿಕಗನędೆಂತುಜೀವವಮು    ಗುಚಿಕಳ್ಳೆರನ^17ಸ್ವೈಬಸ^18ಕೊನ್ಸುಸ^19ತ್ಜೆ ಜಿಲಿ  ^20ಸ್ಥ .. ಕ  ^21ಟಿದವಿ  ^22ರೆಕಣ್ಣಿ  ^23ಕಳ್ಳ^24ನಿಜು^25ಸಿವರಂ ||^26ಕ್ರಿಷ್ಟೆಯೊ^27ಆಳಸಿಗೆಗಾಬಿಯು^28ನಾಡಪ್ಪಿವಿನಸರ^29ಬಿಗೂರುಕೊಡಗೆ^30ಶ್ರಳಯುತೊಜು^31ವಂಣಮುತ್ತಿನಕಳ್ಳರ^32ನಿನಿಸಿಯುಸಫಕ್ಟಿಪರ^33 ಅಲರಕೌನ್ನುತ್ತು  ^34 ಉಳವವಮುಗನಿದೆದ  ^35ಬಿಲ್ಲೇಟೆಂ ||^36ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸವಸ್ತು ಕೂಣ್ಣರೂಲವರಗಂvನ್ನುಗಳಕೋಟ್ಟು ರುಬೀಜಂಗೆ^37ಕೊಡಗಂಯೊಅಲಿಡಿದವಂತಮ್ಮಅನರತುಯುಗೊಣ್ಣ^38ತಣಗೆಳಕವಿಲಿಯುಂಕೊಹೆಗ್ಗಡೆದೇವನಕೋಟೆ ತಾಲೂಕು..

cells.location: *At the same village, on a stone in S'āntayya's field.*
cells.remarks: Praise of the Jina śāsana. While the rājādhirāja mahārāja Kṛishṇa-Rāja-Vāḍeyarayya, seated on the jewelled throne in the city of Maisūr, was ruling the empire of the world :—an elephant having come to Daḷavāyi-kēre and escaped to the forest, Dēvachandraiya, son of Śāntaiya the Amaludār of Heggadadēvankōṭe, having, according to order, had it shot and brought to the presence, received an order for a reward; and dry field (described) assessed at 12 varaha, in the village of Narasimhapura, in the Sāgara hobḷi of the said tāluk, was given to him, marked out by boundary stones, to be enjoyed without hindrance, free of all imposts, by himself, his sons, grandsons and descendants.

maga Dēvachandraiyage yinam agi appane koḍisiddu taloku-paiki Sāgarada hōbali vaḷita Narasimha-

ಅದೇ ಗ್ರಾನ್ಸಕ್ಕೆ ಪಶ್ಚಿಮ ಶಾಂತಯ್ಯನ ಹೊಲದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ,
ಪ್ರಮಾಣ 4' 6" x 2' 4".
ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ
$^{1}$[ಶುಭಮಸ್ತು ಶ್ರೀಮತ್ತುರಾಮಗ^$^{2}$ಂ[ಭೀರಶಾಲ್ವಾಧಾ]ಣೀಕಳಾಧನಂಜಯಾ^$^{3}$ತ್ತ್ರಿಲೋಕ್ಯನಾಥಸೃಸ್ಟ್ಯಾನಸಂಜಿನಾಸನಂ^$^{4}$ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಶ್ರೀವಿಜಯಾಭ್ಯುದಯಶಾಲಿವಾಹನಶಕ[ವರ್ಷ]^$^{5}$ಷ ೧೫೧೧ ವಿರೋಧಿಸಂವತ್ಸರ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕ ಸು ೪ ಭಾನು ॥ ಶ್ರೀಮದ್ವ್ಯಾಧಿರಾ^$^{6}$ಜಮಹರಾಜ[ಶ್ರೀ]^$^{7}$ಕೃಷ್ಣರಾಜಒಡೆಯರವರುಣ್ಯವುನೆಯಸೂರನ^$^{8}$ಗರವಲ್ಲಭತ್ಯಸಿಂಹಾಸನಾರೂಢರಾಗಿಪ್ರತ್ಯುತ್ತಸೌಂಮ್ರಾಜ್ಯಂಗೈಯ್ಯುತ್ತುಂ । ದಳವಾಯಿಚೆಂಗಬ^$^{9}$ಂಡಯುನ್ನುತ್ವಕುತಿಕೊಂಡಹೊಳವಿನಹೊಳಬಳವನ್ನಯ ಅಪ್ಪ, ತೇವವೇರೆಗುಂಬದಿಂದಹೂಡಿ^$^{10}$ಹೋಚಲಗಿನವಸ್ತುಬಗುಹೆಗ್ಗೆದದೇವನಕೋರ್ಟುೀಲವಣದವಾರಾತಂತ್ಯಯವನಗದೇವಚಂ^$^{11}$ದ್ರಯಗಿಯವನಾಗವ್ಯಾಗತೃಕ್ಷತೋಚಿತಿದ್ದ ತಾಲುಕ್‌ಕುಣ್ಯಿಕೆಸಾಗರದೆಹೂಬಳಿವೇತನರ^$^{12}$ಸಿಂಹಪುರದಗ್ಗಾಮ್ಯದವಲ್ಲಿದೇವಲಕಂಡು ಇ.೬ಂ ವರಹಧಧೂಮಿಗೇತಕತಿನ್ಯಕು ಗೂಣಿ^$^{13}$ಲಾಪವೃತ್ತಿ ವನಾಡಿಚೇಕಿಸೆಟ್ಟಿ[ಯೂ]ಯಿಸಲಿಗೇಪ್ಪ ಮಹೋಲಗಿಸಿರೌಂಗುಸಹ ॥^$^{14}$ವಪಹತ್ತಿ ಹೋಲು ಒಕ್ಕ ಕುಳವೇರುನುತುಕಂಗು ೧೫೪ ವೃಭಯಂಹೊನರದು^$^{15}$ವರಹದಜದಲಭೂಮಿಗೇವಿಲಾಯಿಕಾತ್ರಿಕಬ ೧೪ ಸೋಮವಾರದಲೂಲಾಪ^$^{16}$ತ್ರಿವೃ ವನಾಡಿಚೋಯಿತಿನಪತ್ರಪವೃತ್ರಪರಂಪರ್ಯ^$^{17}$ವಾಹಿನೀರುಪಭಿಕಾಸರ್ವ ಮಾನ್ಯವಾಗಿಅಪಶಿಕೋ^$^{18}$೫ಜಿದಕಲ್ಯಾಸನಾ ॥

cells.location: *At the Heggaṇūru (Nemmanahaḷḷi hobli), on a stone in the way to the Māri temple, west of the village.*
cells.remarks: The champion over the three great kings of Chēra, Chōḷa and Pāṇḍya, Chenna-Rāya-Oḍeyar, son of Siṅgappa-Oḍeyar of Kōte, gave to Tapōdeya-Timmaya, the village of Heggaṇūr in the Bayanāḍ- sthala, free of all imposts, for as long as sun and moon endure. Vira Nārāyaṇa gave all within the four boundaries of Heggaṇūr.

ಅದೇ ಹೋಬಳ ಹಗೆಗಿನೂರು ಗ್ರಾಮಕ್ಕೆ ಪಶ್ಚಿಮ. ಮಾಲಿಗೆುಡಿಗೆ ಹೋಗುವ ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ನೆಟ್ಟು ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ.
ಪ್ರಮಾಣ 4' x 3'.
$^{1}$ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಶ್ರೀಸಕಳವಷಾಸ್ತುವಿದಧಾನೇಮಾವಿನವತ್ಸಂಬಂಥೆನೆಯು^$^{2}$ಕೋಳ್ರದನವಸ್ತವತರದರಸಜ್ಯಸ್ತನು ಅನ್ನ್ಯಾನವಾದಸೀಮಾಯೆಹೊನಹಚೇಕೇಲೋ^$^{3}$ಳಪವಂಶೆನ್ನುಮವರುರಾಯಿರಗೊಂದಕೋಠೆಯಿಯಸಂಗಪ್ಪಬಜೆಯಿರಕೌಮಾ^$^{4}$ಳಕೊಂದರಾಯಿಯಪಡೇದುರುತಜದತುತಿಮವಸ್ತ^$^{5}$ನಿಗಿಬಾಯಿನದಹ ಅಜಪೇಗೆ ನುರಾಗ್ಯಾಮವನು^$^{6}$ಶಪ್ಪವ್ಯಾಪ್ವನ್ನಯಿಗೆಕೋಟ್ಯುಳುಚೆದ್ಯನರುರಿಯನಲ್ಲಂ^$^{7}$ನಕಾಳತಪ್ಪಿಪಡೆಗಂಗಯತಡಿಯುಲೀಗೋವ^$^{8}$ಕೊಲಿಂದವಪಹಕ್ಕಿ ಹೋಹೂರುವರಾಸಾಣಿಸಿಯಲಿ^$^{9}$ತಂತಕತೆಯುಯುಕುಕೋಂಡದವನಾಕ್ಕೇ ಹೋಫೂರು^$^{10}$ಕೇತಯು . . . . ತಿಬುರುರುಸಕಳರುಷ^$^{11}$ಸಂದವೆ ೧೪೯೯ ಕೋಧನಸಂವತ್ಸರದ^$^{12}$ಜೇಷ್ಠಪುಸುಂ
$^{13}$ಶ್ರೀವಿೀರನಾ^$^{14}$ರಾಯಣ
$^{15}$ಹಗೆಗಿನೂರ^$^{16}$ಜಾತಸ್ತುಸ್ವವೆ^$^{17}$ಬಳಗಾಗಿ^$^{18}$ಕೋಟ್ಯದೂ

text.location: *At the Heggaṇūru (Nemmanahaḷḷi hobli), on a stone in the way to the Māri temple, west of the village.*
text.remarks:
The champion over the three great kings of Chēra, Chōḷa and Pāṇḍya, Chenna-Rāya-Oḍeyar, son
of Siṅgappa-Oḍeyar of Kōte, gave to Tapōdeya-Timmaya, the village of Heggaṇūr in the Bayanāḍ-
sthala, free of all imposts, for as long as sun and moon endure.
Vira Nārāyaṇa gave all within the four boundaries of Heggaṇūr.Read more (1 KB)

cells.text_roman:
Bhāva-sam[va]tsara-Phālgunada śuddha 10 lū Dēvaprīthi mari-makkal āda Nañjaya-Dēvarige Kariyā-
Vīrayanū Kāṭivālanū bhakti mādida *(usual imprecatory phrases)*
cells.text_original:
ಅದೇ ಹೋಬಳ ಹೋರ್ಲಿಪಾಳ ಗ್ರಾಮದ ಮಾಸ್ತಿ ಗುಡಿಯ ಮುಂದೆ ನೆಟ್ಟ ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ.
ಪ್ರಮಾಣ 2' 10" x 2'.

Footnote
1. ಭಾವವಸಂತವರ್ಷೆಯುಣ
2. ದಿಕುದ್ಧ ಗಂಲೂಅ ದೇವಪ್ರಥಿ
3. ಮರಿವಂೇಷ್ಠ ಕಾವನಂಜಯದೇವ
4. ರೋಗೇಕರಿಯವಿಲರಯಪುನೊಕಾ
5. ಟಿಮಳನೊಭಕ್ತಿ ಮಾಡಿದಯಾ
6. ಧರ್ಮ್ಯಾವನೋಅಲರೊಖ್ಯರೂ
7. ಅನ್ನಿದವರವರವರಾಣಾ
8. ಸಿಯಲ್ಲಿಸಾಸೀರಕವಿಲೀಯು
9. ಕೊಂ ದೊದೋಳಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋದ್ರೂ

cells.remarks: Distinguished at all times for valour in the midst of the battle-field against the desperate attacks of the enemy's force, destroyer of mighty foes, his strong right arm united to the lady valour, champion over hosts, wrestler with hostile forces, wrestler in border warfare, the son of Mārasiṅga, the binder of his relatives, sun in the sky of the Kovale-kula, a fire to the enemy, ruler of Poku-nāḍ and ruler of Kilke-nāḍ, Maleyarāma of Kuṇḍatūr, for the god Nañjuṇḍēśvara of Poku-nāḍ and Kilke-nāḍ united, presented certain land (described), making it over to Balasakti-Jiyar, son of Buvanasakti-Jiyar.
cells.text_roman:

ಹೆಗ್ಗದದೇವನಕೋಟೆ ತಾಲೂಕು,

10. ಲಿಯುಮ್ನಾದಪಾಧ್ಯ್‌ಕಾಣಾಡಕಿ
11. ಲ್ಲಾ ನಾಡಅಳ್ಳೆ೯ಸಂಜ್ಞೆಜಿಲ್ಲೆಕ್ಕೇ೯
12. ಮೋಡೆಮ್ಯೆಗೆ೯ ರಾಳಸಕವ
13. ಕಿರಸಾಯಿರದೊಂಥ

text.remarks:
Distinguished at all times for valour in the midst of the battle-field against the desperate attacks
of the enemy's force, destroyer of mighty foes, his strong right arm united to the lady valour,
champion over hosts, wrestler with hostile forces, wrestler in border warfare, the son of Mārasiṅga,
the binder of his relatives, sun in the sky of the Kovale-kula, a fire to the enemy, ruler of Poku-nāḍ and

cells.location: *At Kittūr (Nemmanahaḷḷi hobli), on a stone in front of the Rāmēśvara temple.*
cells.remarks: An adulteress with black waving curls,¹ an adulteress with full-moon face, an adulteress with endless side glances, an adulteress with compressed lips, an adulteress with adorned slim body, (? was) this (storeyed) mansion,—the double Bayal-nāḍ.² 74 Heggadadevankōte Taluq. While, entitled to the five great drums, the mahā-maṇḍalēśvara, a great lord of heroes, a Triuētra in war, sun among the hill chiefs, a lion of the Kadambas, a fire of destruction to ? Valli, in virtue a Rādhēya, mighty in energy, a fearless Rāma, practising the science of politics, lover of gifts, united to justice, severe to the evil, favourite of his friends, his head at the feet of Vishnu, lord of the Banavāsi rājya, devoted to Mahēsvara, the mahā-maṇḍalēśvara rājādhirāja, the ? nāḍiga of Bira-Bayal-nāḍ, ? Kaudavamma, was ruling the five 300 of Bayal-nāḍ as one kingdom :—Būḍapāḍi ? Pāṇḍya-nāyaka, of Terumaṅgala, the Puṇṇāḍ officer of ? Kēraḷa-nāḍ, ..... .... the Puṇṇāḍ officer of ? Kaudavamma-nāḍ, and the Puṇṇāḍ officer who was the Kikki-nāḍ officer, while carrying on their government, — (after the date), for the god Ravi-Yamēśvara of Kittūr, which was the royal residence, the immense great city Kirttipura, made a grant in Kannevoḷa for the ceremonies and illuminations, and giving the fixed revenue of Maḷchere, the rice heap of Kittūr, the rice heap of Mattige, the rice heap of Kaḍale, the rice heap of Jayapura, the rice heap of Posavoḷalu, and the rice heap of Kaḍalāvaḷi, with pouring of water at the feet of the god, gave the ? oversight to Ravinalla-Dēva and to Ki-iḍākki-Gāvuṇḍa, together with the local rights, and set up this stone. Witnesses,—Kittadiyūr Permmāḍi-Gāvuṇḍa of Saragūr, the farmers of Sāgara, the farmers of Mūḍaga, the ruler of Kuṇḍatūr-nāḍ, Beṅgeyūr Permmāḍi-Gāvuṇḍa, Maṇali Satyavākya-Gāvuṇḍa, Kōṭe Rāchamalla-Gāvuṇḍa. The writing of Araparasa, the sēnabōva. Footnote 1. The earth (or a country) is sometimes called an adulteress because she has a succession of lovers, that is, kings or rulers. 2. This appears to be meant for a verse in the chhappadi-gīta metre, but goes on from the middle of the 3rd line to the middle of the 4th with no intervening word or space.

All the learned Brahmans of Sāgare, the chaturvēdi-maṅgala of Baya-nāḍ, having shown the copper śāsana of their agrahāra to Tipparasa-ayya of Śivanasamudra,—Tipparasa-ayya, having made request to Narasanna-Nāyaka-Voḍeyar, by his order, Tipparasa-ayya made a grant of the village of Sāgare, with its hamlet Bichanahalli, assigned for the upkeep of the tank, altogether two villages, (with all rights and dues pertaining thereto), free of all imposts.

cells.text_original:
1ಶ್ರೀಗಣಾಧಿಪತಯೇನಮಃಅಭುವಸ್ತು ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಶ್ರೀಜಯಾಭ್ಯುದಯಶಕಲಿವಾ
2ಹನಶಕವರ್ಷ ೧೩೧೧ನೆಯಮೇಲಿಸಂವತ್ಸರಘ್ಣಸಂವತ್ಸರ, ಶ್ರಾವಣ ಬಹು ೧೦ಲು
3ಮಕರಸಂಕ್ರಾಂತಿಪುಣ್ಯಕಾಲದಲ್ಲುದ್ದರಿಂದರಸನಾಯಕಕವ್ರಜೆಯರುದರಜನಿತ್ಯಂ ಫಿಧಾರಾ
4ಬಯುನಾದಪವ್ರಗಳಾಣೆಕಟುವನೇಅಧಿಮಂಗಲವಾದದಸಗೆರೆಯ್ಯ ವ್ರದೂಕೇಶಪವಿದ್ಯ
5ನ್ಯ ಹಾರಜನಂಗಳಿತ್ತಮತ್ಲಾನ್ಹರ ದಾತೊಂಬಚಾಸಾಸನವನನೆಸವಿನಮಯಮದೆತಿಪುರಸಅ
6ಯಿನವರಗೆತೋಜಾಲಗೀತಿಪರಸಅಹುವನವರೂಸರಸನಿನಾಯಕಕವ್ರಜೆಯುರಿಗೆಬೆದ
7ಹೌವನಾದಿಆಳಿನವರಪದಿನತಿಪರಸಅಹುವನವರಯೋವನಾಸಗರಯಮ್ಮುಗ್ರಾ ೧
8ಆಕಾಶಲವಳಿ ಕೀಜೆಯುಬಂಜೆಗೆಳುವಣಿಗೆಬೆಚನನ್ನೆಯ್ಯಯಾಗ್ರಾಮ ೧ ಕೂಡಿಗ್ರಾಮ
9ಎದಡಜಳತಸ್ಮಿನಂಗಾವಮವನಮದರೆ ಯುಕಳಸನೂಹತಿಹಸೀಮಾವನುಸ್ಮಾವಿನಬೀಟಿವಾ
10ಗಿಯೋಾಗ್ರಾಮಮೋಗೆಗೇಳುವವಧಾನಸಕಲಸಂವತ್ಸರಸುಂಕಸಮಯವಿನವುಳಸಕಲತದಾ
11 ಯುಲಯೂಆಳಾಪ್ಪಿವರದಮಹಾದಜನಗಳಿಗೆಳುದುವಿನಾಫಪ್ರರದಸದವವರಮಾನ್ಯಕತಪಿ
12ದವರವರವಾರಕಾಸುಂಗಲಿತ್ತರದಲ್ಲಿಗೊಳುಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಸನತಮವತೇದಂತಯು
13ಗಳನೇಕೊಂದವೇದಪಶೇಷೌಪಹರು || ದಾನಪಾಲನಯೋರ್ಮಧ್ಯೇ ದಾನಾಚ್ಛ್ರೇಯೋನುಪಾಲ
14ಲನಾದಾನಾತ್ಸ್ವರ್ಗಮಾವಾಪೋತಿ ದಾನಾತ್ಪಾಲನಾರಜ್ಯ ತಪವದಂ | ಸ್ವದತ್ತಾಂ ದ್ವಿಗುಣಂಪಂ
15ತ್ಯ್ನ್ನಿಯಪರದತ್ತಾಮನುಪಾಲನಾದತ್ವಾಪಹರಣೇಗಂಧದತ್ತೇ ನಿಷ್ಕಫಲಂಭವೇ
16ತ್ತು | ಸ್ವದತ್ತಾಂವರದತ್ತಾಂ ವಾಮಯೋಹರೇತಿವಸುಂಧರಾಕೃಷಿಪಾರ್ವಮರುಷಹಸಸ್ರ
17ಣಿವಿಮವ್ಯಾಣಾಂಜಾಯತಾತಕೇಮಿ ಶ್ರೀಶ್ರೀರೂಮಾಕ್ಷ ಶ್ರೀಶ್ರೀ

cells.location: *At Agattûru, on a stone in the bed of Holsêkere.*
cells.remarks: The mahā-maṇḍalēśvara Timmere-mahā-arasu of Nandyāla made a grant of the village of Āgatûr— belonging to Kaṇe-nād, within the Kōte-śīme, to Bōla-Nañjeyodēya as a grant for a fort. And Bōla- Nañje-Dēva, having set apart 36 *gadŷāna* in the Āgattûr village for the offerings to the god Nañjuṇ- dēśvara, built a *matha* in Nañjaluguḍi, and granted 14 *gadŷāna* in Murige-Āgatûr for Chenna-Viṟaṇṇa- Vūdeyapa there (i. e. of the *matha*). These two sums, amounting to fifty *varaha* per year, may he enjoy, and live in comfort.

text.text_original: ಅದೇ ಗ್ರಾಮದ ಹೊಳೆಕೆರೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಭೂಮಿಯೊಳಗೆ ಮುಚ್ಚಿ ಕೊಂಡಿದ್ದ ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ,ಪ್ರಮಾಣ 4' 6" × 2' 10".$^1$ವೀರೋದ್ವಿತೀಯತುಸಂವತ್ಸರದನುವೆಕು$^2$ಕುಂ ಒಲು । ತ್ರಿಪುಂಸಮಸಾಮಂಡ$^3$ರೆಕ್ಕವರಂದಯಲಿತಿಂದ್ವರೆಮಾಳತರಸು$^4$ಗಳಂ । ಕೊಟೆಯುಯಿಸಿಮೆಯೊಳಾಗದ | ಕಣೆ$^5$ಯುನಾನಿಶೆಳಗೆಲೆವಗಾಮಳಾಗತೊ$^6$ರಣಯೋಳೇಸೋಲದೇಹೋಜೆಯುನಿಯೋವಳ$^7$ಸೋದದಿಯಾಗಾಗಿಕೂಟೆಯು । ಯಿದಕೆ$^8$ಅವನನ್ನೊಬ್ಬನು ಅಳಿವಿಸುವರುಗೋತ್ಪಮರಂತೊ$^9$ಪುವಾರಸಾನಿಸಯಿಲಿಸಂದೆ . . . . . .$^10$ಯುಕರೊಂದುವಲೆಯೆಶೋಳಯಕ್ಕೆ ವಹಾಗೆ$^11$ಪೂಳಲನಂಜೆದೇವಕರುಣ್ಸಂಒಜೇಶ್ವರದೇವಲಗೆ$^12$ಅಮ್ಮುಪವದೀಗಳತ್ಯಾಗ್ಗಾಮದಲ್ಲಗಿ ಳಿ೬$^13$ಆಲಿಖಿತಮದೇವನಲುಗುದಿನಾಜ್ಯೋಳರನಂ$^14$ಜೇವದೇವಮರುತವನುಕಟಿಅಳಿಲ್ಲಗ್ಗೋಳಉರೆಕಂ$^15$ನವಿರಲೆಣಪುಷೆಜಗಳಮುಖಮಗಿಲಗುತ್ತಾರೃ$^16$ಸಲ್ಲಿಗ ೧ಕೌ ಉಭೆಯುಂಗ ೫ಂ ವರುಹವರುಷಪ್ರತಿಯು$^17$ಅಯಿಯತುಷವರಪನುಅನುಭಯಿಸಿುಕೊಂಡಿಸುಖದಿಪರನುಯಿದ.$^18$ಕ್ಕಿ ಆಳವಿದವರವರುಪಾರಣಸಿಯೊಳಿಹದೇವಳ್ದೆ$^19$ತ್ತು ಕಾಯುಲ್ಲಿಹನೊಂದಪಪಾಕ್ಷೆ$^20$ದೋಸದ

cells.location: *At the same village, on a vîrakal in Lakshmi-Nâraṇayya's field.*
cells.remarks: While Raviyyammarasra, who was a rājādirāja, was ruling the kingdom of Bīra-Bayal-nāḍ :— Kõnguṇi-Gavuṇḍa of Manale, with 300 men, and joined by ? Tāmarekolana, having come forth to kill,— Pelvavva of Magge, the Uyyamma-nāḍ-seṭṭi, coming to Kõnguṇi, begged that he would give him the distinction of an umbrella, . . . . . . . . . . . , but did not kill . . . . Then the Nānādēsi Bramma-Seṭṭi, coming with anger, killed. Kõnguṇi, saying that he (the latter) had slain . . . ., cut down the Uyyamma- nāḍ-seṭṭi, and he departed (this life). His younger brother, Gavuṇḍa-Suvila erected this vīra-kal.

kolana kuḍi iriya baṇdaḍe Maggeyaf Pelvavva Uyyamma-nâdu-seţti Koṅguniya . . ge baṇdu koţeya . .

[Footnote *] *So in the original; but Vilambicha or correctly Vilambi = 920 and Śaka 929 = Plavaṅga.*

text.location: *At the same village, on a vîrakal in Lakshmi-Nâraṇayya's field.*
text.remarks:
While Raviyyammarasra, who was a rājādirāja, was ruling the kingdom of Bīra-Bayal-nāḍ :—
Kõnguṇi-Gavuṇḍa of Manale, with 300 men, and joined by ? Tāmarekolana, having come forth to kill,—
Pelvavva of Magge, the Uyyamma-nāḍ-seṭṭi, coming to Kõnguṇi, begged that he would give him the
distinction of an umbrella, . . . . . . . . . . . , but did not kill . . . . Then the Nānādēsi Bramma-Seṭṭi,
coming with anger, killed. Kõnguṇi, saying that he (the latter) had slain . . . ., cut down the Uyyamma-
nāḍ-seṭṭi, and he departed (this life). His younger brother, Gavuṇḍa-Suvila erected this vīra-kal.Read more (1 KB)

cells.remarks: Basavappayya, minister of the mahārājādhirāja rāja-paramēśvara, champion over the mustaches of the world, Kaṭhāri-Sāluva vīra-Krishṇa-Rāya, made a grant of the Sōgehalli village of the Bayi- nāḍ-stala, within the Kōṭa-sīme which belonged to his chiefship, for the decorations of the Rāmēśvara- liṅga of Matakere, in order that the merit might accrue to Krishṇa-Rāya-mahārāya. And within the four boundaries of this village, he granted the rents, customs, and all other rights, free of all imposts.
cells.text_roman:

śri-vīra-Kriṣṇa-Rāyara pradhānar ada Basavap-pyyanavaru tamma nāykatanakke saluva Kōte-
simeya volagana Bayi-nāda sthalada Sogehaliya-grāmamanu Kriṣṇa-Rāya-mahārāyarige dharmmav
āgal .endu Basavapp-ayyanavaru Matakereya Rāmēśvara-liṅgana aṅga-bhōgakke saluv āgi koṭṭev āgi yi-
grāmakke saluva chaluś-simoyal iha 13.. adayasuṅkasameya-modalada sakala-svāmyavanu sarvva-
mānyav āgi koṭṭa grāma yi-grāmakke tappidavaru
akshaya-sukam i-dharmmama- | n i-kshisi rakshisūva puṇya-puruṣargg akkum |
bakshisuv-ātam saṁta- | nā-kṣhayam āyuḥ-kṣhayam [ ...... ] ||

ಅದೇ ಹೋಬಳ || ನೋಗಳ್ಳ ಗ್ರಾಮದ ಮಾರೇ ಗುಡಿಯ ಬಳಿ ನೆಟ್ಟ ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ.

ಶ್ರೀಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸಮ್ಯಾದಿತ್ಯಮಂಡಲೋಪಭೋಗಯಮಂ
ಪಲೋಪಚಾರಿಕವರವುಶ ೧೫೫೯ಸೆಯೂತತ್ಪ್ರಭುಸಂವತ್ಸರದ
*ಅಸ್ಗ್ಯಿಯಜುಸು ೧೧ಲುಬೃಹಸ್ಪತ್ಯಾಸಾರಾಧಿರಾಜರಾಜಪರಮೇ
*ಸ್ವರಪೂಚಿನೀಮಿಸಾರಗಡೇಕತಾರಿಸಾಲಪತ್ಮಿವೇನಿಕಸ್ತಪರಾಯ
*ರೌಪಧಾನರಾದಟಗಸವದ್ಯನ್ಯುವನವರುಕಮನ್ನಾಯ
*ತನಕ್ಕೆ ಸಲುವರೊಕೇಟಿಸೀಮೆಯುಪ್ರಾಣಿಗಣಬಿಯನಾ
^ಜಸ್ಮಾದನೋಗ್ರಹಹಯಾಮಾವನುಶ್ಯಪ್ಪ ರಾಯಮು
®ಹಾರಯಿದಿಥವ್ಯರಾಗಳೆಂವಬುವನವಪೇಳ್ಬೆ
*ಸಿನರುಮವಕರೇಯರಾಯಮೇಸ್ವರಗೆಲೀರಂಗಲಂಗ
೧೦ಭೋಗೇಕಳಿ ಸಲುವಾಗಿಕೊಟ್ಟೆ ವ್ಯಾಗಿವಾಕ್ಕಸಲು
^ವೇಚತುಸ್ಸಿಮೆಯುಲಯೇ೧೪ ಅಡಾಯಾಸುಂಕಸೇವು
೧೨ಯಮಿಯೇದಲಪಾಸಕಲಸಮ್ಯಾವನುಸಮ್ಯಾವೂ
೧೩ಸ್ವಮ್ಯಾಗಿಕೊಟ್ಟ್ಯಗ್ರಾಮಮೂಯಾಗ್ರಾಮಕ್ಕೆ ತಪ್ಪದೆವರು
೧೪ಅಕ್ಷಯಾಸುಂಕವಿನಧರ್ಮ್ಯಾವಪನಿಕ್ಷಿಸೀ ರಕ್ಷಿಸುವ
೧೫ಪುಣ್ಯಪುರುಷರ್ಗಕ್ಕಣ್ಮಲಕ್ಷ್ಮಿ ಸುಪವಾತನಸಂ
೧೬ತಾನನೈಯಯುಯುಕ್ತಯುದಗಂಗೆಯಲಿಗೋ೯
೧೭ಉಖ್ಯಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣರವರುಕೂಂದಪಹಾಪಕ್ಕೆ ಹೂೕಗುವರು

cells.location: At the same village, on a vīrakal in Patel Kencha-nāyaka's yard.
cells.remarks: When Iravi-Challamma was the king of Bīra-Bayal-nāḍ, and Jakkayya of Posavolal was the nād ruler's gāmuṇḍa ;—Harima, (the officer) of Bāukiyarasa, besieged and attacked Posavolalu and its Heggadadevankôte Taluq. 77 hamlet Sôgepaḷḷi,—when Sôvayya ṇālu-ṣeṭti, son of Êchayya of Sôgepaḷḷi, released the cows of Belūrapalli from imprisonment, and fighting, died. *(Verse).* When besieged by fully a hundred horsemen and a thousand six hundred foot soldiers, he released the cows from prison,........ of Sôgepaḷḷi, and driving away and slaying, went to the world of gods.
cells.text_roman:
Svasti Saka-varsham 1029 neya Sarvvajit-samvatsarada Vaiśākka-māsad aṁdu Iravi-Challamma Bira-Bayal-nādan arasu-geyye Poṣavolala Jakkayya nādałvana gāmuṁdanandu Baṅkiyarasana Harima
Hosavolalumam Poṣavolāla palli Soġe-haliyumam mutti erivāgal Soġepallikāra Eebāyyana magaṁ
Sōvayya nādu-seṭti Belurapalli turavumam sereyumam pereg ikki kādi sattam ||
kanda || nejre nūru-kudure sāyira- 1 d arunūr al verasu mutti turuvum sereyam |
perag ikki Sōġepalliya 1 yere ...... su talt irida deva-lōkake vōdam ||
maṁgulam ||

ಅದೇ ಗ್ರಾಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಪಟ್ಟಲ ಕೊಂಕನಾಯಕನ ಮನೇ ಅಂಗಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಗನೇ ವೀรกಲ್ಲು.
^ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸಕಳವತ್ಸರಂ ೧೧೫೯ನೀಯವತ್ಸರಜಂಭ್ರತದವ್ಯಸಕ
*ಮಾಸದವಸ್ತು ಇರವಿಶೆಟ್ಟಮ್ಮಬಿರೇಬಲ್ಲಾಳ ಜನಸರಗೊಣ್ಣೊಪೊನ
*ಪ್ರಭುಲಜಕ್ಕ ೬ನ್ಯಾನಾಹಣ್ಯನಾಗವಣ್ಣನನ್ನ ಬಂಕುಯರಸನ
^ಹರಮಹೋಪೆವೆಳಲಮಂ
*ಪಿನವಿಪಳಲವೊ? ಸೂಗೊಡಜ್ಞೆ
*ಯುವಮುಂಬತ್ತಿ ಇಜವೀವಗಳ
"ಸೊಗೇಪಲ್ಲೆ ಕಾಜಪವಶೆವ್ಯನಮಂಗಂ
^ಸೋನೆವೆಟ್ಟಿನಾಡುಸೆಟ್ಟಿವ್ಯೆಲೊಣ್ಣರಪ್ಪಣಿಯೊಯುವಮಂಜಿಜೇ
*ಗಿಕ್ಕಿ ಕಾವಿಸತ್ವಂ ೧ ಕಣ್ಣಿ | ನೆಜೆನೋಟಾಕು
೧೦ಪುಲೈಸಾಯಿರದಜುನೂಜಾಳ್ಕೆ ರ
ಸುಮವತಿ ತರುವನ್ವೆಂಜೆಮೆಯಂ
ವೆಜಗಿಕಿ ಸೊಗೇಪಲ್ಲೆ ಯುಯೋಜೆ
. . . ಸುಂತಬೆಟ್ಟು ಅರಿಮದೇವೇಲೋೀ
^ಸ್ವ್ಯ ಪೋದಂ || ಮಂಗಳಂ

text.text_original: ಅದೇ ಗ್ರಾಮದ ಮಲ್ಲೇಶ್ವರ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನದ ಬಳಿ ಇರುವ ಕಲ್ಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ.ಹಳಗನ್ನಡ ಹಕ್ಷರ.1 ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಸಿ್ರೀಮತ್ತುಪೃಥಿವಿಸಾಮ್ರಾಜ್ಯಕವೋಡೆಯಿ2 . . ಟ್ಟಿಗೆ . . ವೆಂಕಟಆಯುಸ್ಥನೋಪನೋಲೆಗೋಅಯುಸನ್ನಲ್ಲಿ3 . . . ಗನಿಕೃಷ್ಠಿಾ ನಕ್ಷತೃವಿಚ್ಚಿಪಟ್ಟು . . ಬರುವಮಣಿ4 . . . ವರನಾಶಿಸಿನ್ನಿ ಇನ್ಸಾಮೀ ವ್ಯರೂಮವಾನ್ಮನ್ಯ ಸ್ಪಸಾಧಾನಾ ಅಜೋಕ5 ಡೋವಿಧ್ಯಕೃತ್ನೀರ್ಥಿಾ ದೋರಾನಿಯದಿದದೇಶಸ್ಥ ಮ್ವ್ಯಗಣ್ಣೋ ಏಪ್ಪಾ ಪವಿಯೋಪಿನ6 ತಾವೋಯಾಕೃಟ್ಗಿನೂಳಬೋಟಮದೋಯಿಎನ್ಮದಾನಾಬೋಕ . ಬೋಕ್ಮಲ್ಲ7 ಪ್ಬೋಾತ್ತಿ ವಿಕ್ರಮೃದಿದದೇಕಸುಮಗದೂೕವೋಹದರು . ನವೇದಕಂ

cells.location: *At Mugudlu (Nemmanahaḷḷi hobli), on a stone in the yard of the Nilakanthisvara temple.*
cells.remarks: While S'ivamâra was ruling the kingdom of the world :—Vedirun having ascended to *svarga* *(i. e. died),* a grant was made, according to custom, for worship. Whoso resumes this is guilty of the five great sins. The rent at that time was one *kaḷaga*. The order for rice-land at that time was one *kaḷaga*. The authority over the god's land ? belongs to Vândâra. *(Imprecations).*
cells.text_roman: Svasti srimat-Sivamaram prithuvi-rajyara keya Vedirun svargatt-ereya mariyadi kottan sebige vittar idan alitton pancha-maha-pataka-samyyuktan appon andina tere ekolgam (back) andina key-vesan ekolgam deva-mannu vandara erettaname adan alitton pancha-Varanasi sasirvvaru vrammanarum sasira-kavileyuman kondon appon okkalul pottin makkal puttelkam puttidovum purigain
cells.text_original:
[ವಿಭಾಗ]
1 ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿಶ್ರೀಮತ್ಪತೀವಮಾರಂ
2 ಪ್ಭುವಿರಾಮ್ಯಂಕೋಯೆವಡಿ
3 ರುನಸ್ಸುರ್ತಗತಿ ಜೀವಿಯಮರಿಯಾದಿ
4 ಶೂಲ್ಯೂನಸಜಿಗೋನಿತ್ಯೇರ್ಕದನುಯೋತೀಣ್
5 ಜುಮಣ್ಯ ಮಹಾವತಕಸಂಯುಕ್ತನ
6 ಹಸ್ಮಿನಿಲ್ಗನತೆಯೀಪಕೊಳಂಗ

7 ಅನ್ಸಿ ನಾಕಯ್ಯನಸಿಕೋಳ್ಯ
8 ದೇವಮನ್ನು ವಾನೃದೆಯೀ
9 ತ್ತ ನವೋಲದಾನಸಲೆಯುಕ್ಕಿ ಸಮ್ಪದ್ನಾ
10 ವರನಾಸಿಪಾಸಿಪ್ಯರೂ ವಮ್ಯಣ್ಕಾಜರು
11 ಸುನಿಸಿರವೆಲೋಯುವಮನಕೋನ್ಯೋನ
12 ಅಷ್ಮ ನಬೆಕ್ಕ್ ಲೋಜ್ಯಿ ತಿ ನೃಕ್ಷ್ಮಳಿಪಿ
13 ಟ್ಟಿ ಲ ಪ್ರುಷ್ಠಿ ದೋಮಪುರಣ್ಯ

cells.location: *At Bappanahalli (Heggadadevankote hobli), on a stone in Ammanemma's field.*
cells.remarks: While the Vishnuvardhana pratāpa-chakravartti, the Hoysala strong-armed vīra-Balḷāla-Dēvarasa was carrying on the kingdom of the world :-Heggade-Dēva,—son of the subduer of Nilagiri, dharādhī- rāja, champion over those who have new Rājēndra-Chōla titles, a bull among heroes, protector of re- fugees, Perumāla-Dēvarai-Dēva of Kaneyāla,—made a grant of Boppanahalli in Neyale-nāḍ, as the Perumālupura-agrahāra, together with all the rights of hill possession and all the offerings, free of all imposts, with the privilege of mortgage, sale or gift,—granting for the god Gōpīnātha, the chief god Heggadadevankote Taluq. 79 of the village, two shares, and for Brahmans of various gotras 24 shares, altogether 26 shares, to be maintained as a gift of merit by his own posterity and the posterity of the Brahmans as long as sun and moon endure. And the order for that Perumālupura, that Heggade-Deva set up on a stone below Hosapēṭe and the Tālandoge channel. (Imprecations). That Heggade-Deva's approval, śri-Allālanātha. This is free of all imposts. The writing of Ponnayya, son of Siripati.

Svasti sri Saka-varusha 1249 sandu Prabhava-samvatsarada Chayitra-sudda 9 lu srimad-Vishnu-
vardhana pratapa-chakravartti Hoyisala bhuja-bala sri-Vira-Ballala-Dev-arasaru prithvi-rajyam madutt
iralu srimatu Nilagiri-sadhara dharadhiraja Rajendra-Chola-hosa-birudara-ganda gandara-guli mare-
vokkara kava Kaneyala Perumalu-Deva-Rai-Devanavara makkalu Heggade-Devanu Nevale-nada Bop-
panahalliyanu Perumalupura-agraharav agi a-vura chatus-sime-olagada gadde-beddalu-akshini-agami-
nidhi-nikshepa-jala-pashana-stavara-jangama-siddha-sadhya-ashta-bhoga-tejas-svamya-samasta-bali-sa-
nhita sarvva-namasyav agi adhi kraya-danangalu saluvant agi sa-hiranyodakadindavii dhara-purvvakam
madi gramadhidevate Gopinatha-devarige vritti 2 nana-gotrebhyo brahmanebhyah dattam madidu-
dake vritti 24 antu 26 vrittiyanu sudharmadindavu tamma santati brahmanara santati paramparey-
agi chandrarkar ullanna pariyant agi palisutiru a-Perumalupurakke selav agi a-Heggade-Devanavaru
Hosapeteya Talandoreya kaluveya kelage kallu nattu kottaru gadde Gopinatha-devaringe vritti 2 kke
sa 2 *(11 lines following contain names, &c. of vrittidars)* antu gadde sa 27 nu dhara-purvvakam madi
kotta sasana mangalam aha sri sri

dana-palanayor madhye danat sreyonupalanam |
danat svargam avapnoti palanad achyutam padam ||
vaka-dattam mano-dattam adbhir dattam na diyate |
shashti-varusha-sahasrani vishthayam jayate krimih ||
*(usual final verses)* a-Heggade-Devanavara oppa sri-Allalanatha | idu sarvvamanyam | Siripatiya maga
Poonayyana baraha

[Footnote *] * So in the original; but S'aka 1420=Kalayukti, Bahudhanya = 1440.

130 Heggadadevankote Taluq.

text.location: *At Bappanahalli (Heggadadevankote hobli), on a stone in Ammanemma's field.*
text.remarks:
While the Vishnuvardhana pratāpa-chakravartti, the Hoysala strong-armed vīra-Balḷāla-Dēvarasa
was carrying on the kingdom of the world :-Heggade-Dēva,—son of the subduer of Nilagiri, dharādhī-
rāja, champion over those who have new Rājēndra-Chōla titles, a bull among heroes, protector of re-
fugees, Perumāla-Dēvarai-Dēva of Kaneyāla,—made a grant of Boppanahalli in Neyale-nāḍ, as the
Perumālupura-agrahāra, together with all the rights of hill possession and all the offerings, free of
all imposts, with the privilege of mortgage, sale or gift,—granting for the god Gōpīnātha, the chief god

Heggadadevankote Taluq.	79

of the village, two shares, and for Brahmans of various gotras 24 shares, altogether 26 shares, to be
maintained as a gift of merit by his own posterity and the posterity of the Brahmans as long as sun
and moon endure. And the order for that Perumālupura, that Heggade-Deva set up on a stone below
Hosapēṭe and the Tālandoge channel. (Imprecations). That Heggade-Deva's approval, śri-Allālanātha.
